translations.text: The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, inside the tent of the covering, on the first day of the second month in the second year after they had left the land of Egypt, and said to him:
“Begin by counting the entire congregation of the Israelites, by their tribes and their ancestral households, listing their names one by one.
Count every male twenty years old and above, everyone who goes out with Israel’s army, according to their military divisions.
You and Aaron are to count them.
With you there shall be one of the leaders from each tribe, men belonging to their ancestral households.
These are the names of the men who came with them: from Reuben, Elizur son of Shedeur;
from Simeon, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai;
from Judah, Nahshon son of Amminadab;
And from Issachar, Nethanel son of Zuar.
from Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon;
from the descendants of Joseph: from Ephraim, Elishama son of Ammihud, and from Manasseh, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur;
from Benjamin, Abidan son of Gideoni;
from Dan, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai;
And from Asher, Pagiel son of Ocran.
from Gad, Eliasaph son of Reuel;
from Naphtali, Ahira son of Enan.
These are the chosen men of their camps, the representatives of their tribes. According to their clans, they are the leaders of Israel.
Moses and Aaron took these men who had been named individually.

They assembled the entire congregation on the first day of the month in the second year. They counted them by their kinship groups and their tribes, listing their names, every male twenty years old and above, one by one,
as the Lord had commanded Moses. They counted them at Mount Sinai.

The descendants of Reuben, Israel’s firstborn, were listed by their kinship groups, their clans, and their ancestral households, with their names counted one by one: every male twenty years old and above, everyone who went out with the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Reuben was 46,500.

And the descendants of Simeon, according to their clans, their families, and their ancestral households, counted by name and individually: every male twenty years old and over, everyone able to go out with the army;
The number counted from the tribe of Simeon was 59,300.

The descendants of Judah were listed by their kinship groups, their clans, and their ancestral households, with their names counted one by one: every male twenty years old and above who went out with the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Judah was 74,700.

The descendants of Issachar were listed by their kinship groups, their clans, and their ancestral households, with their names counted one by one: every male twenty years old and above, everyone who went out with the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Issachar was 54,400.

The descendants of Zebulun were listed by their kinship groups, their clans, and their ancestral households, with their names counted one by one: every male twenty years old and above, everyone who went out with the army.
The number counted from the tribe of Zebulun was 57,400.

Among the descendants of Joseph, the descendants of Ephraim were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older, everyone who went out with the army;
the number of those from the tribe of Ephraim was 40,000 plus [?].

The descendants of Manasseh were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older, everyone who went out with the army;
the number of those from the tribe of Manasseh was 32,200.

The descendants of Benjamin were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older, everyone who went out with the army;
the number of those from the tribe of Benjamin was 35,400.

The descendants of Gad were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older, everyone who went out with the army;
the number of those from the tribe of Gad was 45,750.

The descendants of Dan were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older, everyone who went out with the army;
Those counted from the tribe of Dan were 72,700.

The descendants of Asher were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older who went out with the army;
the number of those from the tribe of Asher was 41,500.

The descendants of Naphtali were listed by their families, their clans, and their fathers’ households, by the number of their names, individually: every male twenty years old and older, everyone who went out with the army;
the number of those from the tribe of Naphtali was 53,400.
This was the census taken by Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of Israel, twelve men, one man from each tribe, belonging to the tribes of their fathers’ households.
The total number of the Israelites, together with their forces, twenty years old and older, everyone in Israel who went out to war, was 603,550.
But the Levites, together with their ancestral tribe, were not counted among the Israelites.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Only you shall not count the tribe of Levi or include their number among the Israelites.

“Appoint the Levites over the tabernacle of the testimony, over all its equipment, and over everything inside it, so that they carry the tabernacle and all its equipment and serve in it. They shall camp around the tabernacle.
When the tent is being moved, the Levites shall take it down; when the tent is to remain in place, they shall set it up. Anyone from another clan who joins them in this work shall die.
The Israelites shall camp, each man with his companion and each man with his division, according to their armies.
The Levites shall camp all around the tabernacle of the testimony, so that no guilt comes upon the Israelites. The Levites shall fulfill their duty concerning the tabernacle of the testimony.”
The Israelites did everything that the Lord commanded Moses and Aaron; that is what they did.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:

The Israelites shall camp, each man according to his division and his banner, and according to their fathers’ households. The Israelites shall camp facing the tabernacle of the testimony, all around it.
Those who camp first, toward the sunrise, shall be the camp of Judah with their forces. The leader of the descendants of Judah is Nahshon son of Amminadab;
those counted in his force were 74,700.
The tribe of Issachar shall camp behind them. The leader of the descendants of Issachar is Nethanel son of Zuar;
With his army, those counted were 54,400.
the tribe of Zebulun shall camp behind them. The leader of the descendants of Zebulun is Eliab son of Helon;
With his army, those counted were 57,400.
All those counted in the camp of Judah, with their armies, were 186,400. They shall set out first.
The camp of Reuben shall camp on the south side with their forces. The leader of the descendants of Reuben is Elizur son of Shedeur.
With his force, those counted numbered 46,500.
The tribe of Simeon shall camp beside them. The leader of the descendants of Simeon is Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
With his force, those counted numbered 59,300.
The tribe of Gad shall camp beside them. The leader of the descendants of Gad is Eliasaph son of Reuel.
With his army, those counted were 45,750.
All those counted in the camp of Reuben, with their forces, numbered 151,450. They shall set out second.
The tent of testimony shall set out with the camp of the Levites in the middle of the camps. They shall set out in the same order in which they camp, each following his own leader.
The camp of Ephraim shall camp on the west side with their forces. The leader of the descendants of Ephraim is Elishama son of Ammihud.
With his force, those counted numbered 40,000 plus [?].
The tribe of Manasseh shall camp beside them. The leader of the descendants of Manasseh is Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
With his force, those counted numbered 32,200.
The tribe of Benjamin shall camp beside them. The leader of the descendants of Benjamin is Abidan son of Gideoni.
With his force, those counted numbered 35,400.
All those counted in the camp of Ephraim, with their armies, were 108,100. They shall set out third.
The tribe of Dan shall camp beside them with their forces on the north side. The leader of the descendants of Dan is Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
With his force, those counted numbered 72,700.
The tribe of Asher shall camp beside them. The leader of the descendants of Asher is Pagiel son of Ochran.
With his force, those counted numbered 41,500.
The tribe of Naphtali shall camp beside them. The leader of the descendants of Naphtali is Ahira son of Enan.
With his force, those counted numbered 53,400.
All those counted in the camp of Dan numbered 157,700. They shall set out last, according to their order.
This was the number of the Israelites according to their ancestral households. The total number in their camps, with their armies, was 603,550.
But the Levites were not counted with them, as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Israelites did everything just as the Lord commanded Moses. So they camped according to their order, and so they also set out, each with his own tribe and according to their ancestral households.
This is the family history of Moses and Aaron at the time when the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai.
These are the names of Aaron's sons: Nadab his firstborn, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
These are the names of Aaron’s sons, the anointed priests who were ordained to serve as priests.

Nadab and Abihu died before the Lord because they brought unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai. They had no children. Eleazar and Ithamar served as priests with Aaron their father.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Bring forward the tribe of Levi and present them before Aaron the priest, so that they may serve him.
They shall carry out his duties and the duties of the Israelites before the tent of testimony, and perform the work of the tabernacle.
They shall take care of the equipment of the tent of testimony and carry out the duties of the Israelites in all the work of the tabernacle.
You shall assign the Levites to your brother Aaron and to his sons, the priests, for they are my gift, given to me from among the Israelites.

You shall appoint Aaron and his sons over the tent of testimony. They shall attend to their priesthood and everything concerning the altar and what is inside the curtain. If anyone from another family approaches, he shall be put to death.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

Look, I have taken the Levites from among the Israelites in place of every firstborn who opens the womb among the Israelites. As their ransom, the Levites shall belong to me (said the Lord). For on that day I consecrated all the firstborn in the land of Egypt. Every firstborn in Israel, from human beings to livestock, belongs to me, for I am the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai and said to him:
“Count the descendants of Levi by their ancestral houses, their clans, and their family groups. Count every male one month old or older.”
Moses and Aaron counted them at the Lord’s word, as the Lord had commanded them.
These were the sons of Levi by name: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.
These were the names of Gershon’s sons by their clans: Libni and Shimei.
The sons of Kohath by their clans were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.
And the sons of Merari, according to their families, were Mahli and Mushi;
These were the clans of the Levites by their ancestral houses.
To Gershon belonged the clan of Libni and the clan of Shimei. These were the clans of Gershon.
The number counted, including every male one month old or older, was 7,500.
The descendants of Gershon shall camp behind the tabernacle, on the west side.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Gershon was Eliasaph son of Deuel.
The descendants of Gershon were responsible for these things in the tent of testimony: the tabernacle, its covering, and the curtain at the entrance of the tent of testimony;
the hangings of the courtyard, the curtain at the courtyard gate beside the tabernacle, and all its remaining work.
And of Kohath there was one clan of Amram, one clan of Izhar, one clan of Hebron, and one clan of Uzziel.
These were the clans of Kohath. The number of all their males one month old or older was 8,700. They shall carry out the duties concerning the holy things.
The clans of the descendants of Kohath shall camp beside the tabernacle, on the south side.
The leader of the ancestral house of the clan of Kohath was Elizaphan son of Uzziel.
They were responsible for the ark, the table, the lampstand, the altar, all the sacred utensils used in the service, the coverings, and all the work.
The leader over the leaders of the Levites was Eleazar son of Aaron the priest, who was appointed to oversee the duties concerning the holy things.
To Merari belonged the clan of Mahli and the clan of Mushi. These were the clans of Merari.
Their total, according to the census of all their males a month old and older, was 6,050.
The leader of the ancestral household of the clan of Merari was Zuriel son of Abikia. They were to camp beside the tabernacle, on its northern side.

The clans of the descendants of Merari were entrusted with the capitals of the tabernacle’s pillars, its crossbars, its pillars, their bases, all their equipment, and all the work connected with them;
also the pillars around the courtyard, their bases, their stakes, and their ropes.

Those camping in front of the curtained tabernacle, toward the east, were Moses, Aaron, and his sons. They were to keep charge of the sanctuary on behalf of the Israelites. Anyone from another clan who approached was to be put to death.
The total number of the Levites whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command, according to their families—all their males one month old and over—was 22,000.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, “Count all the firstborn males of the Israelites a month old and older, and record their number by their names.
You shall bring the Levites to me—for I am the Lord—in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all the firstborn livestock of the Israelites.”
Moses counted all the firstborn of the Israelites as the Lord had commanded him.
The total of all the firstborn males a month old and older, counted by their names, was 22,273.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Take the Levites in place of all the firstborn of the Israelites, and the livestock of the Levites in place of all their livestock. The Levites shall belong to me, for I am the Lord.
And as the ransom for those 273 firstborn Israelites who exceeded the number of the Levites.
For each one you shall take payment according to your sanctuary double-drachma; you shall take twenty obols to the shekel.
You shall give the gold to Aaron and his sons as the ransom for those who exceed their number.”
Moses took the ransom gold for those firstborn of the Israelites who exceeded the number redeemed by the Levites.
He took 1,365 shekels of gold, according to the sanctuary shekel.
Moses gave the ransom gold for those who exceeded the number to Aaron and his sons, at the Lord’s word, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“Set apart the descendants of Kohath from among the descendants of Levi, according to their clans and their ancestral households,
from twenty-five years old and upward to fifty years old, everyone who enters to perform all the work of service in the tabernacle.
This is the work of the descendants of Kohath in the tent of testimony: the most holy things.
Aaron and his sons shall enter when the camp sets out. They shall take down the screening curtain and cover the ark of testimony with it.
They shall put over it a covering of [?] skin, spread over them a cloth entirely blue, and fit its carrying poles into place.

On the table for the arranged bread they shall spread a cloth entirely purple, and place its dishes, its bowls, its ladles, and its pouring vessels used for pouring libations, together with the bread that is always arranged upon it.
They shall spread a scarlet cloth over it, cover it with a covering of [?] skin, and fit its carrying poles into place.
They shall take a blue cloth and cover the lampstand on which the lamps are lit, its lamps, its snuffers, the implements used to tend it, and all its oil vessels used in its service.
They shall put it and all its utensils inside a covering of [?] skin and place it on its carrying frame.
They shall wrap the gold altar in a blue cloth, cover it on top with [?] skin, and fit its carrying poles into place.
They shall take all the equipment used for the service, put it in a blue cloth, cover it with [?] skin, and place it on its carrying frame.
They shall put its cover on the altar and spread over it a cloth that is entirely purple.

They shall put in it all the utensils they use in their work: the censers, the forks, the bowls, their covers, and all the utensils of the altar. They shall put a covering of [?] skin over it and set it on its carrying frame. They shall take a purple cloth and cover the basin and its stand, put them inside a covering of [?] skin, and set them on their carrying frame.

When Aaron and his sons have finished covering the holy things and all the sacred equipment, when the camp is setting out, then the descendants of Kohath shall come in to carry them. They must not touch the holy things, lest they die. These are the things the descendants of Kohath shall carry from the tent of testimony.

Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, is appointed over the oil for the lamp, the incense that is burned, the daily offering, and the oil used for anointing. He is appointed over the entire tabernacle, over everything in the sanctuary, and over all the work.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
Do not destroy the clan of Kohath's people from among the Levites.
Do this for them so that they may live and not die when they enter the Holy of Holies: Aaron and his sons shall go in and assign each of them his load.
They must not enter suddenly to look at the holy things and die.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take a census of the descendants of Gershon, by their ancestral households and their clans.
Count all those from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old who enter to perform work in the tent of testimony.
This is the work of the clan of Gershon, what they shall do and what they shall carry:
The curtains of the tabernacle, the tent of testimony itself, its covering, the leather covering above it, and the covering for the entrance of the tent of testimony;
The hangings of the courtyard, the entire tent of testimony, the additional parts, all the equipment for their work, and everything with which they work. They shall do the work.
The work of the descendants of Gershon shall be as Aaron and his sons command them, in all their duties and all their work. Register them by name for everything they are to carry.
These are the duties of the descendants of Gershon in the tent of testimony. Their supervisor is Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Count the descendants of Merari by their families and their ancestral households;
From twenty-five years old upward to fifty years old, count everyone who enters service to do the work of the tent of testimony.

These are the things they are responsible for carrying in all their work in the tent of testimony: the frames of the tabernacle, its bars, its pillars and their bases, the coverings, their stands and pillars, and the curtain at the entrance of the tent of testimony;

The pillars around the courtyard, their bases, their pegs, their cords, all their equipment, and all the equipment for their work. You shall register them by name, together with all the equipment they are responsible for carrying.
These are the duties of the clan of the descendants of Merari in all their work in the tent of testimony. They too are under Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
Moses, Aaron, and the officials of Israel counted the descendants of Kohath by their families and their ancestral households;
From twenty-five years old upward to fifty years old, everyone who entered service to work in the tent of testimony.
The number counted by their families was 2,750.
This was the number of the descendants of Kohath, all those who entered service in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command through Moses.
They counted the descendants of Gershon by their families and their ancestral households;
From twenty-five years old upward to fifty years old, everyone who entered service to do the work of the tent of testimony.
The number counted by their families and their ancestral households was 2,730.
This was the number of the clan of the descendants of Gershon, all those who carried things in the tent of testimony, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command through Moses.
They counted the clan of the descendants of Merari by their families and their ancestral households;
All those from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old who enter to perform the work of the tent of testimony.
Their number, by their clans and their ancestral households, was 3,200.
This was the number of the clan of the descendants of Merari, whom Moses and Aaron counted at the Lord's command through Moses.
All the Levites who were counted by Moses, Aaron, and the leaders of the Israelites, according to their clans and their ancestral households—
All those from twenty-five years old up to fifty years old who enter the service to perform the work of carrying the things of the tent of testimony.
those counted numbered 8,580.
At the LORD’s command they were counted, each man according to his work and the load he carried. They were counted as the LORD had commanded Moses.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites to send out of the camp everyone with leprosy, everyone whose semen flows out, and everyone who has impurity in his person.
Whether male or female, they must send them outside the camp, so that they do not defile their camps, where I come among them.
The Israelites did so and sent them outside the camp. Just as the LORD had told Moses, so the Israelites did.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell the Israelites and say to them: If anyone, whether a man or a woman, commits any of the sins that human beings commit, going astray, even unknowingly, and that person repents,
and makes known the sin that person has committed, the repentant person must repay the full value of the property, add a fifth of its value, and return it to the owner of the property.

But if he has no relative to claim it, and there is no claimant to receive repayment, the restitution for his offense belongs to the LORD. He must give it to the priest, besides the sheep with which atonement is made for him.
All the firstfruits that the Israelites bring, and all their vowed offerings that they bring to the LORD, belong to the priest.
Each person’s vowed offering that is given to the priest belongs to him.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said to him:
Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If any man's wife sins and is unfaithful to him,

Someone has slept with her, and she has strayed and committed adultery, without her husband knowing. She has hidden it from him, though she is defiled, and he has no witness to accuse her—or even if she is innocent—
and a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife when she is defiled, or even when she is not defiled a spirit of jealousy comes over him and he becomes jealous of his wife,

that man shall bring his wife to the priest and bring her offering on her behalf: a tenth of an ephah of barley flour. He shall not pour oil over it or put frankincense on it, because it is an offering under the law of jealousy, a memorial offering that brings sin to remembrance.
he must bring her to the priest and make her stand before the LORD.
The priest must take fresh, clean water in an earthenware vessel. The priest must also take dust from the floor inside the curtained tent and put it into that water.

The priest must make the woman stand before the LORD, uncover the woman’s head, and put into her hands the memorial offering, the offering prescribed by the law of jealousy. In the priest’s own hand must be the water of accusation that brings a curse.

The priest must put the woman under oath and say to her: If no one has slept with you, and you have not strayed from your husband or made yourself guilty, be free from this water of accusation that brings a curse.
But if you have been unfaithful to your husband and defiled yourself, and someone other than your husband has slept with you,

The priest must put the woman under this oath of cursing, and the priest must say to the woman: May the LORD make you a curse and wipe you out from among your people, making your thigh waste away and your belly swell.
May this cursed water enter your belly, make your womb swell, and make your thigh waste away. And the woman must say: Amen, amen.
The priest must write this curse in a scroll and wash it off into the water of accusation that brings a curse.
the accursed water of the ordeal shall enter her belly.
The priest must take the jealousy offering from her hands, place the offering before the LORD, and bring it to the altar.
The priest must take a handful from the offering as its memorial portion and put it on the altar. After this, he must make the woman drink that water.

If she has defiled herself and deceived her husband, that bitter, accursed water will enter her belly, make her belly swell, and cause her thigh to waste away. That woman will become a curse among her people.
But if she has not defiled herself and is clean, she will be cleared and will have offspring.
This is the law of jealousy for a woman who has sinned against her husband and defiled herself,
and for a man upon whom a spirit of jealousy comes, so that he becomes jealous of his wife. He shall present his wife before the Lord, and the priest shall carry out this entire law for her.
The man will be free from sin, but the woman will bear her sin.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: If a man or woman makes a special vow to consecrate themselves to the Lord,
they shall abstain from wine and mead. They shall not drink wine vinegar or mead vinegar, nor drink anything made from grapes, nor eat grapes or raisins throughout the days of their vow.
They shall not eat anything made from grapes, including wine made from raisins, or grape seeds or stalks, throughout the days of their vow, during which they consecrate themselves.

They shall not bring a razor near their head until all the days they have vowed to the Lord are completed. They shall be holy and let the hair of their head grow long throughout the days of their vow to the Lord.
They shall not approach any dead person,
not even their father, mother, brother, or sister, so as to become unclean through them when they die, because the vow to their God rests upon their head.
Throughout the days of their vow, they shall be consecrated to the Lord.

But if someone suddenly dies beside them where they are, dying at that very moment, the consecration of their head will become unclean. They shall shave their head on the day they are cleansed; on the seventh day they shall shave.
On the eighth day they shall bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons to the priest at the entrance to the tent of testimony.

The priest shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering. The priest shall make atonement for them because they sinned through contact with the dead person, and shall consecrate their head on that day.

He shall consecrate himself to the Lord for all the days of his vow and bring a year-old lamb as a guilt offering. The previous days shall not be counted for him, because he has defiled the vow concerning his head.
This is the law for the person who has made a vow: On the day they complete the days of their vow, they themselves shall come to the entrance to the tent of testimony.

They shall bring their offering to the Lord: one unblemished year-old male lamb for a burnt offering, one unblemished year-old ewe lamb for a sin offering, and one unblemished ram for a peace offering;
also a basket of unleavened bread made from fine flour, prepared with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil, together with their grain offerings and drink offerings.
The priest shall bring them before the Lord and offer the person's sin offering and burnt offering.
He shall also offer the young goat as their peace offering to the Lord, together with that basket of unleavened bread. The priest shall offer their grain offering and drink offering.
The person who has made the vow shall shave their consecrated head at the entrance to the tent of testimony and put the hair into the fire of the peace offering.

The priest shall take the boiled shoulder from the ram, one unleavened loaf from the basket, and one unleavened wafer, and place them in the hands of the person who made the vow after they have shaved their head.

The priest shall present these as an offering before the Lord. They shall be holy and belong to the priest, together with the breast of the offering and the shoulder of the contribution. After this, the person who made the vow may drink wine.

This is the law for the person who has made a vow to the Lord concerning the offering they shall bring to the Lord for their vow, besides whatever else their means allow. According to the vow they have made, they shall do what they can, following the law of their consecration.”
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell Aaron and his sons, and say to them: This is how you are to bless the Israelites. Say to them:
They shall place my name upon the Israelites, and I am the Lord who will bless them.
May the Lord bless you and keep you.
May the Lord show his face to you and have mercy on you.
May the Lord turn his face toward you and give you peace.
On the day when Moses finished setting up the tabernacle, he anointed and consecrated it and all its furnishings, as well as the altar and all its utensils; he anointed and consecrated them.
And the leaders of Israel brought their offerings—the twelve leaders, each from his ancestral household. These were the leaders of their tribes who had been appointed to govern them.

They brought their offering before the Lord: six fine wagons and twelve oxen, each wagon with two oxen. There was one wagon from every two leaders and one ox from each leader. They brought them before the tabernacle.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take these from them, and let them be used for the work of the tent of testimony. Give them to the Levites, to each according to his work.
And Moses took the wagon and the oxen and gave them to the Levites.
He gave two wagons and four oxen to the descendants of Gershon, according to their work.
And he gave four wagons and eight oxen to the descendants of Merari, according to their work. They were under Ithamar, the son of Aaron the priest.
But he gave none to the descendants of Kohath, because the work with the holy things was assigned to them, and they carried them on their shoulders.
And the leaders brought offerings for the dedication of the altar on the day it was anointed. The leaders brought their offerings before the altar.
The Lord said to Moses, “One leader each day shall bring his offering, each leader on his appointed day, for the dedication of the altar.”
The one who brought his offering on the first day was Nahshon son of Amminadab, the leader of the tribe of Judah.

He brought his offering: one silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
One bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from the flock for a sin offering.
And for a peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Nahshon son of Amminadab.
And on the second day Nethanel son of Zuar, the leader of the tribe of Issachar, brought his offering.

He brought his offering: one silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from among the cattle, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for a peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Nethanel son of Zuar.
And on the third day the leader of the descendants of Zebulun, Eliab son of Helon, brought his offering.
One silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Eliab son of Helon.
On the fourth day, Elizur son of Shedeur, the leader of the descendants of Reuben, brought his offering.
One silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing 70 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for a peace offering, two cattle, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewe lambs. This was the offering of Elizur son of Shedeur.
On the fifth day, Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai, the leader of the descendants of Simeon, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
On the sixth day, Eliasaph son of Reuel, the leader of the descendants of Gad, brought his offering.
One silver plate weighing 130 shekels and one silver basin weighing 70 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil as a sacrifice.
And one gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for a peace offering, two cattle, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewe lambs. This was the offering of Eliasaph son of Reuel.
On the seventh day, Elishama son of Ammihud, the leader of the descendants of Ephraim, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from among the cattle, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Elishama son of Ammihud.
On the eighth day, Gamaliel son of Pedahzur, the leader of the descendants of Manasseh, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Gamaliel son of Pedahzur.
On the ninth day, Abidan son of Gideoni, the leader of the descendants of Benjamin, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Abidan son of Gideoni.
On the tenth day, Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai, the leader of the descendants of Dan, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold bowl weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb as a sacrifice.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two calves, five rams, five goats, and five year-old ewes. This was the offering of Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai.
On the eleventh day, Pagiel son of Ocran, the leader of the descendants of Asher, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one young bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
And for the peace offering, two oxen, five rams, five goats, and five year-old female lambs. This was the offering of Pagiel son of Ocran.
On the twelfth day, Ahira son of Enan, the leader of the descendants of Naphtali, brought his offering.
One silver dish weighing 130 shekels, and one silver bowl weighing seventy shekels, measured by the sanctuary shekel, both filled with fine flour mixed with oil for a grain offering.
And one gold dish weighing ten shekels, filled with incense.
And one young bull from the herd, one ram, and one year-old lamb for a burnt offering.
And one male goat from among the goats for a sin offering.
For the peace offering, two calves, five sheep, five goats, and five ewes, each a year old. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan.
This was the dedication offering for the altar on the day it was anointed, from the leaders of the descendants of Israel: twelve silver platters, twelve silver bowls, and twelve gold dishes.
Each platter weighed 130 shekels, and each bowl seventy shekels. All the silver of these vessels weighed 2,400 shekels, according to the sanctuary shekel.
And twelve gold dishes filled with incense; the total weight of the gold in these dishes was 120 shekels.

All the cattle for the burnt offering were twelve bulls, along with twelve rams and twelve year-old lambs, for the burnt offerings and the grain offerings, and twelve male goats from the flocks for a sin offering.

And for the peace offering, twenty-four oxen, sixty rams, sixty goats, and sixty unblemished year-old female lambs. This was the dedication offering for the altar after its consecration was completed and after it was anointed.

When Moses entered the tent of testimony to speak with him, he heard the voice of the Lord speaking to him from above the mercy seat that was on the ark of testimony, from between the two cherubim. And he spoke with him.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Speak to Aaron and tell him: Set the lamps on the front side of the lampstand, and light all seven of its lamps.”
Aaron did so. He lit the lamps on the side facing the front of the lampstand, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
This was the workmanship of the lampstand: its branches were all of solid gold, and its flowers were entirely solid. He made the lampstand according to the pattern that the Lord had shown Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Take the Levites from among the Israelites and purify them.
“This is what you shall do to purify them: sprinkle them with water of purification. They shall shave their entire bodies and wash their clothes, and they shall be clean.
They shall take one young bull from the herd, together with its grain offering of fine flour prepared with oil. They shall also take a year-old bull from the herd for a sin offering.
You shall bring the Levites before the tent of testimony and assemble the whole congregation of the descendants of Israel.
You shall bring the Levites before the Lord, and the descendants of Israel shall lay their hands on the Levites.
Aaron shall set the Levites apart before the Lord from among the descendants of Israel, and they shall perform the Lord’s service.
The Levites shall lay their hands on the heads of the bulls. He shall offer one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to the Lord, and make atonement for them.
You shall place the Levites before the Lord, before Aaron, and before his sons, and present them as a gift to the Lord.
Separate the Levites from among the Israelites, and they shall be mine.
After this, the Levites shall enter to do the work of the tent of testimony. You shall purify them and present them before the Lord.
For they have been given to me as a gift from among the Israelites. I have taken them for myself in place of everyone who first opens the womb, all the firstborn of the Israelites.
For every firstborn among the Israelites is mine, both human and animal. On the day when I killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, I set them apart as holy for myself.
I have taken the Levites in place of every firstborn among the Israelites.

I have presented the Levites as a gift, and they have been given to Aaron and his sons from among the Israelites, to perform the service of the Israelites in the tent of testimony and to make atonement for the Israelites, so that no one among the Israelites approaches the holy places.
Moses, Aaron, and the whole assembly of the Israelites did this to the Levites. Just as the Lord commanded concerning the Levites, so the Israelites did to them.
The Levites purified themselves and washed their clothes. They were presented to Aaron as a gift before the Lord, and Aaron made atonement for them to purify them.
After this, the Levites entered to perform their service in the tent of testimony before Aaron and his sons. Just as the Lord commanded Moses concerning the Levites, so they did to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
This is the rule concerning the Levites: from twenty-five years old and upward, they shall enter to perform their work, the service of the tent of meeting.
From the age of fifty, he shall retire from his work and shall no longer serve.
His brother shall serve in the tent of meeting and keep their charge, but they shall not perform the labor. This is how you shall deal with the Levites concerning their respective duties.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the first month of the second year after they had left the land of Egypt, and said to him:
Tell the Israelites to observe the Passover at its appointed time.
On the fourteenth day of the first month, toward evening, you shall observe it at its appointed time. You shall observe it according to its law and its commandment.
Moses told the Israelites to observe the Passover.
They began observing it on the fourteenth day of the month in the wilderness of Sinai. Just as the Lord commanded Moses, so the Israelites did.
Some men came who were themselves unclean and could not observe the Passover that day. They came before Moses and Aaron that same day.
Those men said to them, “We are people who have uncleanness upon us. Let us not be excluded from bringing the Lord’s offering among the Israelites at its appointed time.”
Moses said to them, “Wait here, and I will hear what the Lord commands concerning you.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell the Israelites and say to them, “If anyone is unclean through a human corpse or is in a distant land, whether among you or among your descendants, they shall observe the Lord’s Passover.
They shall observe it in the second month, on the fourteenth day of the waxing moon, toward evening. They shall eat it with unleavened bread and bitter herbs.
They shall leave none of it until morning, nor shall they break any of its bones. They shall observe it according to the law of the Passover.

But if a person is clean and is not in a distant land, yet neglects to observe the Passover, that person shall be cut off from their people, because they did not bring the Lord’s offering at its appointed time. That person shall bear the guilt of the sin.

If a foreigner comes to you in your land, he shall observe the Lord’s Passover. They shall observe it according to the law of the Passover and its commands. There shall be one law for you, both for the foreigner and for the native-born.”
On the day when they set up the tent, the cloud covered the tent, the house of testimony. At night, something with the appearance of fire came over the tent until morning.
This happened continually: the cloud covered it by day, and the appearance of fire by night.
Whenever the cloud rose from the tent, the Israelites would set out afterward. Wherever the cloud stopped, there the Israelites would camp.
At the Lord’s command they would set out. Throughout all the days when the cloud overshadowed the tent, the Israelites remained encamped.
When the cloud remained over the tent for many days, the Israelites kept their charge to the Lord and did not set out.
For as many days as the cloud covered the tabernacle, the Israelites remained camped at the word of the Lord, and at the Lord’s command they set out.
When the cloud remained from evening until morning and lifted at dawn, they would set out during the day.
If the cloud remained for a long time, overshadowing it for a month, the Israelites would remain encamped and would not set out.
For they set out at the Lord’s command and kept the Lord’s ordinances, according to the Lord’s command through Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Make yourself two silver trumpets. Make them of hammered silver. They will serve you for calling the assembly to camp and for making the assembly set out.
When you blow them, the whole assembly shall gather at the entrance of the tent of testimony.
But if you blow only one, all their leaders, the rulers of Israel, shall come to you.
When you sound the signal with them, the camps of those encamped on the east side shall set out.

You shall sound their signal a second time, and the camps of those encamped toward the south shall set out. You shall sound their signal a third time, and the camps of those encamped toward the west shall set out. You shall sound their signal a fourth time, and the camps of those encamped toward the north shall set out. When they are to set out, you shall sound a signal.
When you blow to gather the assembly, blow without sounding the signal.
The sons of Aaron, the priests, shall blow the trumpets. This shall be an everlasting ordinance for you throughout your generations.
If you go out to war against your enemies who are hostile to you, sound the signal with the trumpet. You shall be remembered before the Lord and saved from your enemies.

On your days of rejoicing, at your festivals, and at your new moons, blow the trumpets over your offerings and over your sacrifices of well-being. They shall be a reminder of you before your God. I am the Lord your God.”
In the second month of the second year, on the fifth day of the waning moon, the cloud lifted from the tent of meeting.
The Israelites set out on their journey from the wilderness of Sinai, and the cloud stopped in the wilderness of Paran.
Those who went first set out at the word of the Lord through Moses.
The camp of the people of Judah set out first in their prescribed order, with their forces. Nahshon son of Amminadab was in charge of their forces.
Nethanel son of Zuar was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Issachar.
Eliab son of Helon was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Zebulun.
They took down the tabernacle, and the descendants of Gershon and the descendants of Merari set out with it, carrying the tabernacle.
The camp of Reuben set out in their prescribed order, with their forces. Elizur son of Shedeur was in charge of their forces.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Simeon.
Eliasaph son of Reuel was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Gad.
The descendants of Kohath shall set out carrying the holy things, and they shall set up the tent before their arrival.
The camp of Ephraim set out in their prescribed order, with their forces. Elishama son of Ammihud was in charge of their forces.
Gamaliel son of Pedahzur was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Manasseh.
Over the army of the tribe of Benjamin was Abidan son of Gideoni.
The camp of the people of Dan set out in their prescribed order, behind all the other camps, with their forces. Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai was in charge of their forces.
Pagiel son of Ocran was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Asher.
Ahira son of Enan was in charge of the forces of the tribe of Naphtali.
This was the arrangement of the Israelites’ forces, and they set out with their troops.

Moses said to Hobab son of Reuel the Midianite, Moses’ father-in-law, “We are traveling to the place of which the Lord told us, ‘I will give it to you.’ Come with us, and we will treat you well, for the Lord has promised good things for Israel.”
He said to him, “I will not go. Instead, I will return to my own country and my birthplace.”
He said to him, “Do not leave us, for you have lived with us in the wilderness and grown old among us.
If you go with us, we will share with you all the good that the Lord does for us.”
They traveled from the mountain of the Lord a journey of three days. The ark of the Lord’s law went ahead of them on the three-day journey to find them a resting place.
Whenever the ark set out, Moses would say, “Rise up, Lord! Let your enemies be scattered, and let all who hate you flee.”
When it rested, he would say, “Return, Lord, among the thousands and tens of thousands of Israel.”
The cloud came and shaded them by day as they set out from the camp.
The people complained wickedly before the Lord. The Lord heard and became angry, and fire from the Lord blazed against them and consumed one section of the camp.
The people cried out to Moses. Moses prayed to the Lord, and the fire stopped.
That place was named Burning, because fire from the Lord had blazed against them.
Those who had joined them were seized with craving. They sat down and wept, as did the Israelites, and said, “Who will give us meat to eat?
We remember the fish we used to eat for nothing in the land of Egypt, and the cucumbers, melons, garlic, onions, and leeks.”
But now we are dried up; we have nothing else to look at except manna.
The manna was like coriander seed, and its appearance was like hail.
The people would go about and gather it for themselves. They would grind it in a mill or pound it in a mortar, cook it in a pot, and make it into cakes. Its taste was like honey mixed with oil.
When the dew fell on the camp at night, the manna also fell upon them.
Moses heard them weeping, family by family, each at his own doorway. The Lord’s anger burned fiercely, and Moses too was displeased.
Moses said to the Lord, “Why have you treated your servant so badly? Why have I not found favor in your sight, that you have laid the burden of this people upon me?
Did I conceive all this people? Did I give birth to them, that you should tell me, ‘Carry them in your arms, as one carries a child in one’s care, into the land you swore to their ancestors’?
Where am I to get meat to give to all this people? Look, they are weeping to me and saying, ‘Give us meat to eat!’
I cannot care for this people all by myself, because the burden is too heavy for me.
If this is how you will treat me, please kill me outright, if I have [?] mercy in your sight, so that I may not see my misery.”

The Lord said to Moses, “Gather for me seventy men from among the elders of the Israelites, whom you yourself know to be leaders of the people and their scribes. Bring them into the tent of witness, and let them stand there with you.

I will come down and speak with you there. I will take some of the spirit that is upon you and place it upon them. They will share the burden of this people with you, and you will not have to labor for them alone.

You shall say to the people, “Purify yourselves for tomorrow, and you shall eat meat. For you wept before the Lord, saying, ‘Who will give us meat to eat? We were better off in the land of Egypt.’ The Lord will give you meat to eat, and you shall eat meat.”
You will eat it not for one day, nor for two, nor for five days, nor for ten, nor for twenty days,

but for a whole month, until it comes out of your nostrils and becomes nauseating to you, because you have rejected the Lord who is among you and have wept before him, saying, ‘Why did you bring us out of the land of Egypt?’”
Moses said, “There are six hundred thousand people on foot among whom I live, and you tell me, ‘I will give them meat, and they will eat for a whole month.’
“Can sheep and cattle be slaughtered for them, or all the fish of the sea be gathered for them, to provide enough for them?”
The Lord said to Moses, “Is the Lord’s hand powerless? Now you will see whether my word comes true for you or not.”
Moses went out and told the people the Lord’s words. He gathered seventy men from among the people’s elders and stationed them around the tent.

The Lord came down in the cloud and spoke to him. He took some of the spirit that was upon him and placed it upon the seventy elders. When the spirit rested upon them, they prophesied, but they did not do so again.

Two men remained in the camp. The name of one was Eldad, and the name of the other was Medad. The spirit rested on them too. They had been registered along with the others, but they had not come to the tent, and they prophesied in the camp.
A young man ran and reported to Moses, saying, “Eldad and Medad are prophesying in the camp.”
Joshua son of Nun, who attended Moses and was his chosen one, said to him, “My lord Moses, stop them!”
Moses said to him, “Are you jealous for my sake? If only all the Lord’s people would prophesy when the Lord puts his spirit upon them!”
He and the elders of Israel returned to the camp.

A wind went out from the Lord and carried quail across from the sea, bringing them down into the camp. They extended a day’s journey on either side all around the camp and were spread out two cubits above the ground.

The people stayed up all that day, all night, and all the following day, gathering quail for themselves. Whoever gathered the least gathered ten cors. They spread them out and dried them all around their camp.
While the meat was still between their teeth, before they had finished it, the Lord became angry with the people. The Lord killed people with a very great plague.
That place was named Memorial of Craving, because they buried the people who had craved there.
The people moved from Memorial of Craving to Hazeroth, and they stayed at Hazeroth.
Miriam and Aaron spoke against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman Moses had married, for he had married an Ethiopian woman.
They said, “Has the Lord spoken only to Moses? Has he not spoken to us too?” And the Lord heard.
Now Moses was a very humble man, more humble than anyone else living on earth.
At once the Lord said to Moses, Aaron, and Miriam, “Come, all three of you, to the tent of testimony.”
The Lord came down in a pillar of cloud to the entrance of the tent of testimony. He called Aaron and Miriam, and both came forward.
He said to them, “Listen to my words. If there is a prophet of the Lord among you, I appear to him in a vision and speak to him in a dream.
“But my servant Moses is not like that. He is faithful throughout my house.”
I speak to him mouth to mouth, openly and not in hidden words, and he has seen the glory of the Lord. Why, then, were you not afraid to speak against my servant Moses?
The Lord’s fierce anger came upon them, and they went away.
The cloud withdrew from the tent, and Miriam was stricken with leprosy and became white as snow. Aaron turned toward Miriam, and there she was, stricken with leprosy.
Aaron said to Moses, “I beg you, my lord, do not hold this sin against us, for we did not realize that we had sinned.
“Let us not be like the dead, like a baby coming out of its mother’s womb, with half her flesh eaten away.”
Moses cried out to the Lord and said, “Lord, I beg you, heal her.”
The Lord said to Moses, “If her father had spat in her face, would she not have been ashamed for seven days? Let her be shut out of the camp for seven days, and afterward let her come back in.”
Miriam was shut out of the camp for seven days, and the people did not move on until Miriam was cleansed.
After this, the people set out from Hazeroth and camped in the wilderness of Paran.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Send men as scouts to inspect the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the Israelites to rule over: one man from each of their tribes and from their ancestral clans. You shall send their leaders.
Moses sent them from the wilderness of Paran at the Lord’s command. All these men were leaders of the Israelites.
These were their names: from the tribe of Reuben, Shammua son of Zaccur;
From the tribe of Simeon, Shaphat son of Hori.
from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Issachar, Igal son of Joseph;
from the tribe of Ephraim, Hoshea son of Nun;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Palti son of Raphu;
from the tribe of Zebulun, Gaddiel son of Sodi;
from the tribe of Joseph, from the descendants of Manasseh, Gaddi son of Susi;
From the tribe of Dan, Ammiel son of Gemalli.
from the tribe of Asher, Sethur son of Michael;
from the tribe of Naphtali, Nahbi son of Vophsi;
from the tribe of Gad, Geuel son of Machi.
These were the names of the men Moses sent to explore the land. Moses named Hoshea son of Nun Joshua.
Moses sent them to explore the land of Canaan and said to them, “Go up into that wilderness, and from there go up into the hill country.
Look at the land to see what it is like, and at the people who live in it, to see whether they are strong or weak, few or many.
See what the land they live in is like, whether it is good or bad, and what their towns are like, whether they have walls or not.
See what the land is like, whether it is fertile or dry, and whether there are trees in it or not. When you have looked, take some of its fruit.” It was harvest time, before the grapes were picked.
They went up and explored the land from the wilderness of Zin to Rehob, on the way to Hamath.
They went up through the wilderness and reached Hebron. Ahiman, Sheshai, and Talmai, descendants of Anak, were there. Hebron had been built [?] years before the city of Zoan in Egypt.
They reached the Valley of the Cluster and explored it. There they cut off a vine branch with a single cluster of grapes on it and carried it on a pole. They also took some pomegranates and figs.
They named that place the Valley of the Branch because of the branch the Israelites cut off there.
They returned from there after exploring that land for forty days.

They went and came to Moses and Aaron and the whole assembly of the Israelites in the wilderness of Paran, at Kadesh. They gave their report to them and to the whole assembly and showed them the fruit of that land.
They reported to them, saying, “We reached the land to which you sent us, a land flowing with milk and honey. Here is its fruit.”
The people who live in that land are strong, and its cities are very strongly fortified and large, and they have walls. We also saw the descendants of Anak there.
The Amalekites live in the land toward the south. The Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites live in its mountains, and the Canaanites live toward the sea and along the Jordan River.
Caleb ordered the people to be silent before Moses and said, “No! Let us go up and take possession of it, for we can certainly overcome them.”
But the men who had gone up with them said, “We will not go up, for we cannot go up against that people: they are much stronger than we are.”

They made the land they had explored seem terrifying to the Israelites, saying, “The land we went to explore is a land that keeps [?] those who live in it, and all the people we saw are men of exceedingly great height.”
“There we saw those who [?], and we were like locusts before them; that is also how we appeared to them.”
The whole assembly gathered together and cried out aloud, and the people wept all night.
All the Israelites grumbled against Moses and Aaron, and the whole assembly said to them, “It would have been better for us to have died in the land of Egypt than to die in this wilderness.”
“Why is the Lord bringing us into that land to fall in battle, while our wives and children become captives? It would be better for us now to return to the land of Egypt.”
They said to one another, “Let us appoint a ruler for ourselves and return to the land of Egypt.”
Moses and Aaron fell on their faces before the whole assembly of the Israelites.
Joshua son of Nun and [?] son of Jephunneh, who were among those who had explored that land, tore their clothes.
They said to the whole assembly of the Israelites, “The land we explored is exceedingly good.”
If the Lord has chosen us, he will bring us into that land and give it to us—a land flowing with milk and honey.
“Only do not rebel against the Lord, and do not fear the people of that land, for we will destroy them. Their time has passed, and the Lord is with us. Do not fear them.”
The whole assembly said that they should stone them. Then the glory of the Lord appeared in a cloud at the tent of testimony to all the Israelites.
The Lord said to Moses, “How long will this people reject me? How long will they refuse to believe in me, despite all the signs I have performed for them?”
“Shall I strike them with death and destroy them, and make you and your father's household into a great nation, far more numerous than this one?”
Moses said to the Lord, “The Egyptians will hear of it, those from whose midst you brought this people out by your power.”

“All who live in this land will hear that you, Lord, are among this people, and that you, Lord, appear to them as one is seen face to face. Your cloud stands over them, and you go before them in a pillar of cloud by day and in a pillar of fire by night.”
“If you crush this people as though they were a single man, the nations that hear of your name will say,
‘Because the Lord was unable to bring them into the land he swore to give them, he killed them in the wilderness.’
“Now let your power be exalted, Lord, just as you spoke, saying:

‘The Lord is slow to anger, abundant in mercy, and righteous, forgiving wrongdoing, sin, and error. Yet he will certainly not acquit the offender, and he visits a parent's sins upon the children to the third and fourth generation.’
“Forgive the sins of this people according to the greatness of your mercy, just as you have been merciful to them from the land of Egypt until now.”
The Lord said to Moses, “Look, I have forgiven them, as you said.”
“But as surely as I live and my name lives, the glory of the Lord will fill the whole earth.”
For all the men who saw my glory and the signs I performed in the land of Egypt and in the wilderness have now tested me these ten times and have not listened to my voice.

They will not see the land that I swore to give their fathers, except for their children who are here with me, all those who do not know good and evil, every young child who has no understanding. To them I will give that land. But none of those who despised me will see it.
But my servant Caleb, because he had a different spirit upon him and followed me, I will bring into that land which he entered, and his descendants will inherit it.
The Amalekites and Canaanites live in the lowlands of Aurion. But you must move on and return to the wilderness by the road to the Red Sea.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron, saying:
How long must I listen to the grumbling of this assembly, these children of Israel who grumble against you and have grumbled before me?
Tell them, “As I live, says the Lord, I will certainly do to you in this wilderness just as you have spoken in my hearing.”
Your dead bodies will fall—all of you who were registered and counted, from twenty years old and upward, all of you who grumbled against me.
You will not enter the land in which I raised my hand to swear that I would settle you, except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.
But the children whom you said would become captives, I will bring into that land, and they will inherit the land from which you turned away.
Your dead bodies will fall in this wilderness.
Your children will tend flocks in the wilderness for forty years.

According to the number of days during which they explored that land, forty days, each day will count as a year for you because of your sins. It will be forty years for you, and then you will know the [?] of my anger.
For I am the Lord who has spoken: I will do this to this evil assembly that has joined together against me. In this wilderness they will perish, and there they will die.
When the men whom Moses sent to explore that land returned, they grumbled about it to the whole assembly and spread a bad report about that land.
Those men who said that the land was bad died before the Lord, although the land was good.
Joshua son of Nun and Caleb son of Jephunneh survived from among those men who went to explore that land.
Moses told all the children of Israel these words, and the people mourned deeply.
They rose early in the morning and went up to the top of the mountain, saying, “Here we are. We will go up to the place that the Lord told us about, for we sinned concerning it.”
Moses said to them, “Why are you disobeying the word of the Lord? This is not good for you.
Do not go up, for the Lord is not with you, and you will fall before your enemies.”
For Amalek and Canaan are there before you, and you will fall by the sword because you turned away and rejected the Lord. The Lord is not with you.
They boldly went up to the top of the mountain, but the ark of the Lord’s law and Moses did not move from the midst of the assembly.
The Amalekites and Canaanites who lived on that mountain came down and drove them away as far as Hormah, and they returned to the assembly.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Tell the children of Israel and say to them: When you enter the land in which you will live, which I am giving you,

you are to make an offering to the Lord, a gift or a sacrifice, to fulfill a solemn vow, or as a voluntary offering, or at your festivals, producing a pleasing aroma for the Lord, whether from the cattle or from the sheep.
The person who brings his offering to the Lord must bring a grain offering of fine flour, one-tenth of an ephah, mixed with one-quarter of a hin of oil.
He shall provide a quarter of a hin of wine as a drink offering with the offering or the sacrifice. For each lamb he shall provide this amount as an offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
When you offer a ram as an offering or a sacrifice, you shall make an offering of two tenths of fine flour mixed with a third of a hin of oil.
He shall bring a third of a hin of wine as a drink offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
And if you make an offering or a sacrifice from the cattle, or make a special vow of well-being to the Lord,
he shall bring with that bull a grain offering of three-tenths of fine flour mixed with half a hin of oil.
And half a hin of wine for a drink offering, an offering with a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
This is what you shall do for each bull, each ram, or each lamb from among the sheep or the goats.
According to the number you offer, you shall do this for each one, in proportion to their number.
Everyone who is native-born shall do this, and in this way bring his offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

If there is a foreigner among you who has migrated to your land, or anyone living among your descendants, who makes an offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, your congregation shall do just as you yourselves do for the Lord.
There is one law for you and for the foreigners living among you, an everlasting law throughout your generations. The foreigners shall be just as you are before the Lord.
There is one law and one rule for you and for the foreigner living among you.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: When you enter the land to which I am bringing you,
when you eat the food of that land, you shall set apart a special contribution for the Lord from the first of your dough.
You shall set apart a loaf as a contribution to him. Just as you set apart a contribution from the threshing floor, so you shall set one apart for him from the first of your dough.
You shall give a contribution to the Lord throughout your generations.
If you sin and do not carry out all these commandments that the Lord spoke to Moses,
as the Lord commanded you through Moses, from the day the Lord commanded you and before then, throughout your generations,

If something has escaped the notice of the assembly, the whole assembly shall offer one unblemished bull from the herd as a sacrifice with a pleasing aroma to the Lord, together with its grain offering and its drink offering according to the law, and one male goat from the goats as a sin offering.

the priest shall make atonement for the whole congregation of the Israelites, and they shall be forgiven, because it was done unknowingly. They have brought their offering and sacrifice to the Lord for their sin before the Lord and for their unwitting offense.
The whole congregation of the Israelites and the foreigner who comes among you shall be forgiven, because the whole people acted unknowingly.
If one person sins unknowingly, that person shall bring a year-old female goat as a sin offering.
The priest shall make atonement before the Lord for the person who sinned unknowingly, for that person's unwitting offense, and shall make atonement on that person's behalf.
For the native-born among the Israelites and for the foreigner living among you, there is one law when someone acts unknowingly.
But anyone who acts defiantly, whether native-born or a foreigner, has provoked the Lord by this. That person shall be removed from among their people.
Because that person has sinned against the word of the Lord and transgressed his commandment, that person shall be utterly destroyed, and their sin shall remain upon them.
While the Israelites were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering wood on the Sabbath day.
Those who found him brought him to Moses and Aaron and to the whole congregation of the Israelites.
They kept him in custody, because there was no ruling about what they should do to him.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, “That man must be put to death. The whole congregation shall stone him with stones.”
The whole congregation brought him outside the assembly and stoned him, as the Lord had told Moses.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Tell the Israelites and say to them that they are to make tassels on the edges of their garments throughout their generations, and put a twisted blue cord in the tassel at the edge.

It shall be on your tassel, so that you may look at it and remember all the Lord’s commandments and obey them. Do not follow your own thoughts and your own eyes, after which you go astray in unfaithfulness,
so that you may remember and obey all my commandments and be holy to your God,
who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God. I am the Lord your God.”
Korah son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, opposed him, along with Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On son of Peleth, son of Reuben.
They stood against Moses, together with two hundred and fifty men from among the Israelites, leaders of the assembly, chosen for the council and men of renown.

They rose up against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “Enough from you! The entire congregation is holy, every one of them, and the Lord is among them. Why do you set yourselves above the Lord’s assembly?”
When Moses heard this, he fell on his face.
He said to Korah and all his assembly, “Let the Lord look and recognize those who belong to him, and bring his holy ones near to himself.
Do this: take censers for yourselves, Korah and all his assembly.
Put fire in them and put incense on them before the Lord tomorrow. The man whom the Lord chooses shall be holy for the descendants of Levi.”
Moses said to Korah, “Listen to me, descendants of Levi!

Do you regard it as a small thing that the God of Israel chose you from the assembly of Israel and brought you near to himself to do the work of the Lord’s tabernacle and to stand before the assembly and serve it?
He brought you near, together with your brothers, the descendants of Levi, and you want to become priests as well!
Thus you and all your assembly have rebelled against the Lord. And what is Aaron, that you should grumble against him?”
Moses sent for Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, but they said, “We will not come.
Do you regard it as a small thing that you brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey, that you have killed us in the wilderness, so that you may rule over us?

Are you a ruler as well? Have you brought us into a land flowing with milk and honey? Is this the inheritance you have given us in the wilderness, and vineyards? Are these the eyes of those men that you have gouged out? We will not come.”
Moses was deeply distressed and said to the Lord, “Do not look favorably on their offering. I have taken nothing desirable from any one of them, and I have not harmed even one of them.”
Moses said to Korah, “Consecrate your assembly, and be ready before the Lord tomorrow—you, they, and Aaron.
Let each one take his censer, and put incense in it. Let each one bring his censer before the Lord.”
Each one took his censer, and they put fire and incense in them. Moses and Aaron stood at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
Korah gathered all his assembly against them at the entrance to the tent of testimony, and the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole assembly.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“Withdraw from among this assembly, and I will destroy them all at once.”
They fell on their faces and said, “Lord, God of every spirit and all flesh, if one man has sinned, will the Lord’s wrath come upon the whole assembly?”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell the congregation to move away from the area around Korah’s tent.”
Moses got up and went to Dathan and Abiram, and all the elders of Israel went with him.
He spoke to the congregation and said to them, “Move away from the tents of these wicked men, and do not touch anything belonging to them, so that you are not destroyed because of all their sins.”
They moved away from the area around Korah’s tent. Dathan and Abiram came out and stood at the entrances of their tents, together with their wives, their children, and their possessions.
Moses said, “By this you will know that the Lord sent me to do all these things, and that I did not act on my own initiative:
if these men do not die as other people die, and their punishment is not like the punishment of other people, then the Lord has not sent me.

But if the Lord displays an opening of the earth, and the earth opens its mouth and swallows them, their households, their tents, and everything belonging to them, and they go down alive into Sheol, then they will know that these men have provoked the Lord.”
When he had finished speaking all these words, the earth split beneath their feet.
The earth opened and swallowed them, their households, all the people who were with Korah, and their wives.
They and everything belonging to them went down alive into Sheol. The earth covered them, and they perished from among the congregation.
All the Israelites around them fled at the sound of their cries, saying, “Otherwise the earth may swallow us too!”
Fire came out from the Lord and consumed the 250 men who had brought incense.
The Lord said to Moses and to Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest:

“Pick up the bronze censers from among those who were burned, and scatter this foreign fire away from here, because the censers of these men, who sinned at the cost of their own lives, have become holy.
Make them into hammered plates to be used for the altar, because they were brought before the Lord and became holy. They shall be a sign to the Israelites.”
Eleazar son of Aaron took all the bronze censers that those who were burned had brought, and they made them into material for the altar,

as a reminder to the Israelites that no one from another family, who is not a descendant of Aaron, may come forward to offer incense before the Lord, lest he become like Korah and his company, just as the Lord had spoken through Moses.
The next day the Israelites complained against Moses and Aaron and said to them, “You have killed the Lord’s people!”
When the congregation assembled against Moses and Aaron and followed them to the tent of testimony, the cloud immediately covered it, and the glory of the Lord appeared.
Moses and Aaron went to the front of the tent of testimony.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
“Move away from the midst of this congregation, and I will destroy them all at once.” They fell on their faces.

Moses said to Aaron, “Take a censer, put fire from the altar in it, place incense on it, and bring it quickly into the congregation. Make atonement for them, because wrath has already gone out from before the Lord and has begun to destroy the people.”
Aaron took it as Moses had told him and ran quickly into the congregation. The plague had already begun among the people. He put on the incense and made atonement for the people.
He stood between the dead and the living, and the plague stopped.
Those who died in the plague numbered fourteen thousand seven hundred, besides those who died because of Korah.
Aaron returned to Moses at the entrance to the tent of the testimony, and the plague stopped.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
