“Speak to the Israelites and take from them a staff for each ancestral household, from all the leaders of their ancestral households, twelve staffs. Write each man’s name on his staff.
Write Aaron’s name on Levi’s staff, for each tribe of their ancestral houses shall give one staff.
Place them in the tent of the testimony, before the testimony, where I appear to you.
The staff of the man I have chosen will sprout, and I will put an end to all the Israelites’ grumbling against you.”
Moses spoke to the Israelites, and all their leaders gave him staffs, one staff for each leader according to their ancestral households, twelve staffs. Aaron’s staff was among their staffs.
Moses placed those staffs before the Lord in the tent of the testimony.

On the following day, Moses and Aaron entered the tent of the testimony, and there Aaron’s staff, belonging to the house of Levi, had sprouted. It had put out leaves, blossomed with flowers, and produced almonds.
Moses brought all their staffs out from before the Lord to all the Israelites. They looked, and each man took his staff.
The Lord said to Moses, “Place Aaron’s staff before the testimony, to be kept as a sign for the children of those who do not obey. Let their grumbling against me stop, so that they do not die.”
Moses and Aaron did everything the Lord commanded Moses; that is what they did.
The Israelites said to Moses, “Look, we are finished! We are being destroyed and are perishing!
For everyone who approaches the Lord’s tent dies. Are we then to die completely?”
The Lord spoke to Aaron and said to him, “You and your sons and your father’s household with you shall bear the guilt associated with your priesthood.
Bring your brothers also, the tribe of Levi, your father’s people, near to you. They shall join you and serve you, while you and your sons with you attend to the tent of the testimony.
They shall carry out your duties and the duties of your tent. But they must not approach the sacred utensils or the altar, so that neither they nor you die.
They shall join you and carry out the duties of the tent of the testimony, doing all the work of the tent. No one from another family may approach you.
You shall carry out the duties concerning the holy things and the altar, so that wrath will no longer come upon the Israelites.
I have taken your brothers, the Levites, from among the Israelites. They have been given as a gift to the Lord to do the work of the tent of the testimony.

You and your sons with you shall guard your priesthood according to every law concerning the altar and what is inside the curtain, and perform the service that is the gift of your priesthood. Anyone from another family who enters shall die.

The Lord said to Aaron, “Look, I have given you charge of the first offerings brought to me, from everything the Israelites consecrate to me. I have given it to you until you [?], and after you to your sons, as an everlasting ordinance.”

This shall be yours from the sacrifices consecrated as most holy: all their offerings, all their sacrifices, all their offerings for repentance, and all their offerings for sins. Everything they bring to me from all the holy things belongs to you and your sons.
Eat it in the most holy place. Every male shall eat it—you and your sons—for it is holy to you.

This shall also be yours: the first portion of their gifts and of everything the Israelites bring in. I have given it to you and to your sons and daughters with you as a lasting ordinance. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
All the first portions of oil, all the first portions of wine, and the first portions of wheat—everything they bring to the Lord—I have given to you.
All the firstfruits of the grain from all their land, and everything they bring to the Lord, I have given to you. Everyone in your household who is clean may eat it.
Everything devoted to God among the Israelites belongs to you.

Every firstborn that opens the womb among all living creatures, everything they bring to the Lord, from humans to animals, belongs to you. But the firstborn of humans must be redeemed with a ransom, and you must also redeem the firstborn of unclean animals.
Its redemption price, from one month old, is five shekels according to the sanctuary shekel, which is twenty obols.
But you must not redeem the firstborn of cattle, sheep, or goats, because they are holy. Pour out their blood at the altar, and offer their fat as a sacrifice to the Lord, a pleasing fragrance.
Its flesh shall be yours, like the breast they bring as an offering and like the right shoulder; it shall be yours.

All the sacred offerings that the Israelites set apart for the Lord I have given to you, to your sons, and to your daughters with you, as an everlasting law and a perpetual ordinance. It is everlasting before the Lord for you and your descendants after you.
The Lord said to Aaron, “You shall inherit none of their land, and you shall have no share among them, because I am your share and your inheritance among the Israelites.”
“As for the descendants of Levi, I have given them the Israelites’ tithes as their share, in return for all the work they perform in serving the tabernacle.
The Israelites must no longer enter the tabernacle, so that they do not incur guilt that brings death.

The Levites shall perform this service of the tent of testimony, and they shall bear their sins. This is an everlasting ordinance throughout their generations, and they shall inherit no inheritance among the Israelites.
For I have given the Israelites’ tithes—all the offerings they set apart for the Lord—to the Levites as their share. Therefore I told them, ‘You shall have no inheritance among the Israelites.’”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:

“Speak to the Levites and tell them, ‘When you receive from the Israelites the tithe that I have given you from them as your share, you too shall set apart from it an offering to the Lord: a tenth of the tithe.
Your offering shall be credited to you like wheat from the threshing floor and like an offering from the winepress.
Likewise, you too shall set apart an offering to the Lord from all your tithes, from everything you receive from the Israelites. From it you shall give the Lord’s offering to Aaron the priest.
Bring all that they offer first; from it [?] shall be consecrated.
Tell them, “When you set aside some of the firstfruits, it shall be counted for the Levites as grain from the threshing floor and as wine from the winepress.”
You and your households may eat it anywhere, because it is your payment in return for your service in the tabernacle.
You shall incur no sin on account of it, because you take its first portions out of it. Do not defile the Israelites’ holy offerings, so that you do not die.’”
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said to them:
This is the commandment of the whole law that the Lord commanded, saying, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them to bring you a red heifer, pure and without blemish, on which no yoke has been placed.
Give it to Eleazar the priest. They shall take it outside the camp to a clean place and slaughter it before him.
Eleazar shall take some of its blood and sprinkle its blood seven times in front of the tabernacle.
They shall burn it in his presence. They shall burn its hide, its flesh, and its blood together with its dung.
The priest shall take cedar wood, hyssop leaves, and scarlet material, and they shall throw them into the fire in which the heifer is burning.
The priest shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water. Afterward he may enter the camp, but the priest shall be unclean until evening.
The one who burned it shall also wash his clothes and bathe his body, and he shall be unclean until evening.

A clean man shall gather its ashes and deposit them outside the camp in a clean place. They shall be kept for the Israelites’ camp for water of sprinkling; they shall keep them because they use it for purification.
The one who gathers the heifer’s ashes shall wash his clothes and be unclean until evening. This shall be an everlasting law for the Israelites and for the foreigners living among you.
Anyone who touches the dead body of any human being is unclean for seven days.
In this way he shall purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, and he shall be clean. But if he does not purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, he shall not be clean.

Anyone who touches the corpse of any human being who has died and does not purify himself defiles the Lord’s tabernacle. That person shall be cut off from Israel, because the water of sprinkling has not been sprinkled on him. He is unclean, and his uncleanness still remains upon him.
This is the law concerning a person who dies inside a house: everyone who enters that house and everyone who is inside the house is unclean for seven days.
Every open vessel that has no covering fastened over it is unclean.
Anyone who touches, out in the countryside, someone who has been killed, a corpse, a human bone, or a grave is unclean for seven days.
For that unclean person they shall take some of the ashes of what they burned for purification, and mix fresh water with them in a vessel.

They shall bring hyssop leaves, and a clean man shall dip them into that water and sprinkle it on the house, on its furnishings, on every person who was there, and on anyone who touched a human bone, someone who was killed, a corpse, or a grave.

The clean person shall sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and on the seventh day, and shall purify him on the seventh day. He shall wash his clothes and bathe his body in water, and he is unclean until evening.

If a man becomes unclean and does not purify himself, that person shall be removed from among the assembly, because he has defiled the Lord’s sanctuary. Because the water of sprinkling has not been sprinkled on him, he is unclean.
This shall be a lasting law for you: the person who sprinkles the water of sprinkling shall wash his clothes, and anyone who touches the water of sprinkling is unclean until evening.
Everything that comes into contact with an unclean person becomes unclean, and anyone who touches it is unclean until evening.
The Israelites, their entire assembly, arrived in the wilderness of Zin in the first month, and the people stayed in Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.
There was no water for the assembly, and they gathered against Moses and Aaron.
The people quarreled with Moses and said to him, “It would have been better for us to die when our brothers died before the Lord!
Why have you brought the Lord’s assembly into this wilderness to kill us and our livestock?
Why have you brought us out of Egypt to bring us into this evil place—a place where nothing is sown, where there are no figs, no vineyards, no pomegranates, and no water to drink?”
Moses and Aaron went away from the assembly to the entrance of the tent of testimony and fell on their faces. The glory of the Lord appeared to them.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:

“Take that staff and gather the assembly, you and your brother Aaron. Speak to the rock before them, and it will give its water. You shall bring water out of the rock for them and give the assembly and their livestock water to drink.”
Moses took the staff from before the Lord, as the Lord had commanded him.
Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly before that rock, and he said to them, “Listen to me, you rebels! Are we to bring water out of this rock for you?”
Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with that staff. A great deal of water came out, and the assembly and their livestock drank.
The Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not believe so as to show my holiness before the Israelites, you shall not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”
This is the water of dispute, because the Israelites quarreled before the Lord.
Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to the king of Edom, saying, “This is what your brother Israel says: You yourself know all the suffering that has come upon us.
Our ancestors went down to Egypt and lived in Egypt for many days, and the Egyptians oppressed us and our ancestors.
We cried out to the Lord, and the Lord heard our voice. He sent his angel and brought us out of Egypt. Now we are in the city of Kadesh, on the border of your land.

Let us pass through your land. We will not pass through fields or vineyards, and we will not drink water from wells. We will travel along the main road and will not turn aside to the right or to the left until we have passed beyond your territory.
Edom said to him, “You must not pass through my land. Otherwise, I will come out to meet you, and we will fight.”
The Israelites said to him, “We will pass along the mountains. If we or our livestock drink any of your water, we will pay you its price. This is nothing; we will only pass along the mountain.”
He said, “You must not pass through my land.” Edom came out to meet him with a large force and a strong hand.
Edom refused to let Israel pass through his territory, so Israel turned away from him.
They set out from Kadesh, and the Israelites, the whole congregation, camped at Mount Hor.
The Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, near the border of the land of Edom, saying:
“Let Aaron be gathered to his people, for you will not enter the land that I have given to the Israelites, because you rebelled against me at the waters of dispute.
Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
Remove Aaron’s garments from him and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there.”
Moses did as the Lord commanded him, and he brought them up Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.
He removed Aaron’s garments from him and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron died there on the summit of the mountain, and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.
The whole congregation saw that Aaron had passed away, and the whole house of Israel wept for Aaron for thirty days.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the wilderness, heard that Israel had come by the road to Atharim. He attacked the Israelites and took some of them captive.
Israel made a vow to the Lord and said, “If the Lord delivers this people to me, I will devote them and their towns to destruction.”
The Lord heard Israel’s voice and delivered the Canaanites into their hands. They devoted them and their towns to destruction, and they named that place Hormah.
They set out from Mount Hor toward the road to the Red Sea and went around the land of Edom. The people became impatient along the way.
They complained against the Lord and Moses and said to him, “Why did you bring us out of Egypt to kill us in this wilderness? There is no food and no water, and we are sick of this worthless bread.”
The Lord sent snakes among the people, which killed them and bit them, and many of the Israelites died.
The people came to Moses and said to him, “We have sinned, because we complained against the Lord and against you. Now pray to the Lord, so that he will remove the snakes from us.”

Moses prayed to the Lord for the people. The Lord said to Moses, “Make yourself a snake and place it where it can be seen. Whenever a snake bites someone, let everyone who has been bitten look at it and live.”
Moses made a bronze snake and set it up where it could be seen. Whenever a snake bit someone, that person looked at the bronze snake and lived.
The Israelites set out and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Iye-abarim, on the other side, in the wilderness facing Moab toward the sunrise.
They set out from there and camped in the valley of Zered.
They moved on from there and camped beyond the Arnon, which flows from the mountains of the Amorites, for it is the boundary of Moab, lying between Moab and the Amorites.
Therefore it says in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: “He set Zoom ablaze
and established the stream of the Arnon, which is at Ar, which is called the boundary of Moab.”
From there they came to the well—the well about which the Lord told Moses, “Gather the people, and I will give them water to drink.”
At that time Israel sang this song at the well: “Lead the singing to it! The well
that the princes dug, that the kings of the nations hewed out under their rule.” From that well they went to Mattanah.
From Mattanah they went to Nahaliel, and from Nahaliel to Bamoth.
From Bamoth they went to Anapen, which is in the wilderness of Moab, near the summit of the structure that overlooks the wilderness.
Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites with a peaceful message, saying,

“Let us pass through your land. We will follow the road and will not turn aside into fields or vineyards. We will not drink water from your wells. We will travel along the main highway until we have passed beyond your territory.”
Sihon would not allow Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people and went out into the wilderness to fight Israel. He reached Jahaz and fought against Israel.
Israel killed them with iron weapons, and his land became theirs, from the Arnon to the Jabbok, as far as the Ammonites, for Jazer is the boundary of the Ammonites.
Israel took all those cities, and Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites, in Heshbon and throughout its territory.
For there in Heshbon were the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites. He had previously fought against the king of Moab and taken all his land from Aroer to the Arnon.
Therefore the makers of riddles say: “Go to Heshbon, so that it may be built and the cities of Sihon established.
For fire came out of Heshbon, and a flame from the cities of Sihon. It consumed as far as Moab and swallowed up the monuments of the Arnon.
Woe to you, Moab! You destroyed the people of Chemosh who returned, but you saved their sons. Their daughters were taken captive to Sihon king of the Amorites.
Heshbon wiped out their descendants as far as Dibon, and their women still kindled a fire against Moab.”
Israel lived in all the cities of the Amorites.
Moses sent men to inspect Jazer. Then they captured it along with its towns and drove out the Amorites who were there.
They turned and went up along the road to Bashan. Og king of Bashan came out with all his people to meet them and fight against them at Edrei.

The Lord said to Moses, “Do not be afraid of him, for I will deliver him, all his people, and all his land into your hands. You will do to him as you did to Sihon king of the Amorites, who lived in Heshbon.”
He killed him, his sons, and all his people, leaving him no survivor, and they took possession of their land.
The Israelites moved on and camped toward the plains of Moab, by the Jordan opposite Jericho.
When Balak son of Zippor saw everything Israel had done to the Amorites,
Moab was very afraid of the people because they were numerous, and Moab was alarmed at the presence of the Israelites.
Moab said to the elders of Midian, “Now this crowd will consume everyone around us, as an ox consumes the grass in the wilderness.” Balak son of Zippor was king of Moab in those days.

He sent messengers to Balaam son of Beor at Pethor, which was by the river in the land of his people, to summon him, saying, “Look, a people has come out of Egypt. They have covered the face of the land and are living near me.

Now come and curse them for me, because they are stronger than we are. Perhaps we can kill some of them and drive them out of the land. For I know that whoever you bless will be blessed, and whoever you curse will be cursed.”
The elders of Moab and the elders of Midian went, taking their divination equipment with them. They reached Balaam and told him Balak’s message.
He said to them, “Stay here tonight, and I will tell you what the LORD says to me.” So the messengers of Moab stayed with Balaam.
The LORD came to Balaam and said to him, “Why have these men come to you?”
Balaam said to the LORD, “Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, sent them to me, saying:
‘Look, a people has come out of Egypt and has covered the face of the land. They are living near me. Now come and curse them for me. Perhaps I can kill them and drive them out of the land.’”
The LORD said to Balaam, “Do not go with them, and do not curse the people, because they are blessed.”
Balaam got up in the morning and said to Balak’s messengers, “Go back to your master, for the LORD has not allowed me to go with you.”
The messengers of Moab got up and went to Balak and said to him, “Balaam refused to come with us.”
Balak again sent messengers, more numerous and more distinguished than the previous ones.
They came to Balaam and said to him, “This is what Balak son of Zippor says: ‘Please do not delay coming to me.
For I will give you great honor, and I will do for you everything you tell me. Come and curse this people for me.’”

Balaam answered Balak’s messengers and said to them, “Even if Balak gave me a house full of gold and silver, I could not go against the word of the LORD and do anything, small or great, of my own will.
Now you too stay here tonight, [?] what the LORD will do, as he speaks to me.”
The LORD came to Balaam at night and said to him, “If these men have come to summon you, get up and follow them. But do only what I tell you.”
Balaam got up in the morning, saddled his donkey, and went with Balak’s messengers.
The LORD’s anger flared up because he went, and the angel of the LORD took his stand to obstruct him. Balaam was riding his donkey, and his two servants were with him.

When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand, she turned aside from the road and went into the open country. He struck the donkey with a stick to make her return to the road.
The angel of the LORD stood between the walls of a vineyard, with a wall on one side and a wall on the other.
When the donkey saw the angel of the Lord, she pressed against the wall and scraped Balaam’s foot. He struck her again.
The angel of the LORD went on again and stood in a narrow place where there was no room to turn aside, either to the right or to the left.
When the donkey saw the angel of the LORD, she knelt down beneath Balaam, and he struck the donkey with a stick.
The Lord opened the donkey’s mouth, and she said to Balaam, “What have I done to you that you strike me? This is now the third time!”
Balaam said to the donkey, “Because you are making a fool of me! If I had a sword in my hand, I would have killed you by now.”
The donkey said to Balaam, “Am I not your donkey, whom you have ridden from your youth until today, this very day? Have I ever been accustomed to treating you this way?” He said to her, “No.”
The LORD opened Balaam’s eyes, and he saw the angel of the LORD standing in the road with a drawn sword in his hand. He bowed down and fell facedown before him.

The angel of the LORD said to him, “Why have you struck your donkey? This is now the third time. Look, I came out to obstruct you, because your way was not right before me. When your donkey saw me, she turned aside from me, and this is now the third time.”
And if she had not turned aside from me, I would certainly have killed you by now, but I would have kept her alive.
Balaam said to the angel of the Lord, “I have sinned, because I did not know that you were standing against me on the road ahead of me. Now, if you do not approve, I will go back.”
The angel of the Lord said to Balaam, “Go with these men, but take care to speak only the words I tell you.” Balaam went with Balak’s messengers.
When Balak heard that Balaam had come, he went out to meet him in the city of Moab on the border of the Arnon, at one end of their territory.
Balak said to Balaam, “Did I not send messengers to summon you? Why did you not come to me? Was I not able to honor you?”
Balaam said to Balak, “Look, I have come to you. Now I can speak the word that God puts in my mouth, and I will take care to speak it.”
Balaam went with Balak, and they entered a walled town.
Balak slaughtered sheep and cattle and sent some to Balaam and to the messengers who were with him.
In the morning Balak took Balaam and brought him up to the monument of Baal. From there he showed him a portion of the people.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build seven altars for me here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your sacrifice, and I will go. Perhaps the Lord will appear before me, and I will tell you whatever he reveals to me.” And Balak stood beside his sacrifice.
Balaam went to inquire of God, going straight ahead. God appeared to Balaam, and Balaam said to God, “I have prepared seven cattle, and they have offered a bull and a ram on the altar.”
The Lord put a word into Balaam’s mouth and said to him, “Return to Balak and say this.”
He returned to him and found him standing beside his sacrifice, with all the messengers of Moab beside him. And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him.
He delivered his oracle and said, “Balak, king of Moab, summoned me from Mesopotamia, from the regions of the east, saying, ‘Come, curse Jacob for me; come, denounce Israel for me.’
“How can I denounce someone whom the Lord has not denounced? And how can I curse someone whom the Lord has not cursed?
“For I see him from the mountain peaks, and I look upon him from the hills. Look, a people who dwell alone and are not counted among the nations!
“Who can know the descendants of Jacob, and who can count the people of Israel? Let my soul die with the souls of the righteous, and let my descendants be like their descendants.”
Balak said to Balaam, “What have you done to me? I summoned you to curse my enemies for me, yet look, he has blessed them abundantly!”
Balaam said to Balak, “Must I not take care to speak everything that the Lord puts into my mouth?”
Balak said to him, “Come with me again to another place, where you will not see them except for one part of them. You will not see them all. Curse them for me there.”
He took him and led him around into the wilderness, to the summit of the hewn rock. He built seven altars and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
Balaam said to Balak, “Stand beside your sacrifice, while I go to inquire of the Lord.”
The Lord met Balaam and put a word into his mouth. He said to him, “Return to Balak and say this.”
He returned to him and found him standing beside his sacrifice, with all the messengers of Moab beside him. Balak said to him, “What did the Lord say?”
He delivered his oracle and said, “Rise, Balak, and listen! Pay attention, Balak; listen, son of Zippor!
“The Lord is not like a human being who can be deceived, nor like a mortal who can be intimidated. Yet you say that he will not act! Will he speak and not fulfill it?
Look, I have come to bless him. I will bless, and it will not be reversed.
“There is no hardship in Jacob, and suffering will not appear in Israel. The Lord his God is with him, and the honor of angels is his.
“God brought him out of the land of Egypt; his glory is like that of a one-horned beast.
“For there is no sorcery in Jacob and no divination in Israel. At each appointed time, Jacob and Israel will be told what the Lord will do.
“Look, a people who rise like a young lion and leap up like a lion! They will not lie down until they eat some of their prey and drink the blood of those they have killed.”
Balak said to Balaam, “Neither curse them for me nor bless them.”
Balaam answered Balak, “Did I not tell you, ‘Whatever the Lord tells me, that is what I will do’?”
Balak took Balaam to the top of Peor, which overlooks the wilderness.
Balaam said to Balak, “Build me seven altars here, and prepare seven bulls and seven rams for me here.”
Balak did as Balaam told him and offered a bull and a ram on the altar.
When Balaam saw that it was good in the Lord’s sight to bless Israel, he did not go, as he usually did, to seek divination before him. Instead, he turned his face toward the wilderness.
Balaam raised his eyes and saw Israel moving tribe by tribe, and the Spirit of God came upon him.
He spoke his saying and said, “Balaam son of Beor says; the man who sees clearly says:
who sees a vision of God, whose eyes are uncovered while he sleeps;
How beautiful are your houses, Jacob, and your tents, Israel!
Like trees that give shade, like a garden beside a river, like tents that the Lord has planted, and like cedars beside water.
A man will come forth from his descendants and rule over many nations. His kingdom will be exalted above Gog, and his kingdom will grow great.
God led him out of Egypt; he has the glory of a one-horned animal. He will devour the nations that are his enemies, drain their fat, and pierce the enemy with his arrows.
He lies down and rests like a lion, like a lion’s cub. Who will wake him? May those who bless you be blessed, and may those who curse you be cursed.
Balak became angry with Balaam and struck his hands together. Balak said to Balaam, “I called you to curse my enemies for me, but look, you have blessed them these three times!”
Now go home. I said I would honor you, but now the Lord has not given you honor.”
Balaam said to Balak, “Did I not tell the servants you sent to me,
‘Even if Balak gave me gold and silver enough to fill this house, I could not go beyond the Lord’s command to do good or evil on my own. Whatever the Lord tells me, that is what I will say’?
Now, look, I am going home. Come, and I will tell you what this people will do to your people in the days to come.”
He uttered his oracle and said, “Balaam son of Beor speaks; the man who sees truly speaks,
who hears the word of God, who knows the strength of the Most High, and who has seen a vision of God, whose eyes are uncovered while he sleeps.

I see him, but not now; I behold him, but he is not near. A star will rise from Jacob, and one will arise from Israel. He will destroy the messengers of Moab and take captive all the descendants of Seth.
Edom will become his possession, and Esau, his enemy, will become his possession. Israel acted with strength.
One will arise from Jacob and destroy those who escaped from the city.”
When he saw Amalek, he uttered his oracle and said, “Amalek was the first among the nations, but their descendants will perish.”
When he saw the Kenites, he uttered his oracle and said, “Your wickedness is strong, and even if you set your nest in a rock,
even if Beor has a nest of cunning, Assyria will take you captive.”
When he saw Og, he uttered his oracle and said, “Alas! Who will live when God does this?
One will come forth from the hands of the Kittim. They will afflict Asshur and afflict the Hebrews, and they too will perish together.”
Balaam got up, went away, and returned home. Balak also went home.
The Israelites stayed in Shittim, and the people became defiled and committed sexual immorality with the daughters of Moab.
They invited them to the sacrifices of their gods, and the people ate their sacrifices and bowed down to their gods.
Israel devoted itself to Baal of Peor, and the LORD’s anger flared up against Israel.
The LORD said to Moses, “Take the leaders of the people and hang them up before the LORD in the sunlight, so that the LORD’s fierce anger may turn away from Israel.”
Moses said to the people of Israel, “Each of you must kill the men of your household who have served Baal of Peor.”

Just then, a man from among the Israelites came and took his son to a Midianite woman, before Moses and before the whole congregation of the Israelites, while they were weeping at the entrance to the tent of testimony.
When Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, saw this, he rose from among the congregation and took a spear in his hand.
He went in after the Israelite man into the chamber and pierced both of them, the Israelite man and the Midianite woman, through her belly. Then the plague stopped among the Israelites.
Those who died in the plague numbered twenty-four thousand.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said:

“Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, has turned my anger away from the Israelites, because he was zealous for me with my own zeal among them. So I did not destroy the Israelites in my jealousy.
Therefore I say: I hereby give him my covenant of peace.
It will be a covenant of everlasting priesthood for him and his descendants after him, because he was zealous for his God and made atonement for the Israelites.”
The name of the Israelite man who was killed was Zimri son of Salu, a leader of an ancestral house of Simeon.
The name of the Midianite woman who was killed was Cozbi daughter of Zur, leader of the people of Samoth. He belonged to an ancestral house of Midian.
The LORD spoke to Moses and said, “Speak to the Israelites and tell them:
‘Treat the Midianites as enemies and kill them,

because they too treat you as enemies through deceit and through all the schemes they use against you in the matter of Peor and in the matter of Cozbi, daughter of the leader of Midian, their sister, who was killed on the day of the plague because of Peor.’”
After the plague, the Lord spoke to Moses and to Eleazar the priest and said to them:
“Take a new census of the whole congregation of the Israelites, twenty years old and above, by their ancestral houses—all those in Israel able to go to war.”
Moses and Eleazar, who was with him, spoke to them on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, and said to them:
“Those twenty years old and above, as the LORD commanded Moses.” Now the Israelites who came out of Egypt were:
Reuben, Israel’s firstborn. The descendants of Reuben were Hanoch and the clan of the Hanochites; from Pallu, the clan of the Palluites;
from Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; and from Carmi, the clan of the Carmites.
These were the clans of Reuben, and their number was forty-three thousand seven hundred and thirty.
The son of Pallu was Eliab.
The sons of Eliab were Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These were leaders of the assembly; they were the ones who rose against Moses and Aaron in Korah’s assembly when they opposed the Lord.
The earth opened its mouth and swallowed them and Korah. He and their assembly died when fire consumed the 250, and they became a warning sign.
But the sons of Korah did not die.
And the descendants of Simeon: from Nemuel, the clan of the Nemuelites; from Jamin, the clan of the Jaminites; and from Jachin, the clan of the Jachinites.
From Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites; and from Shaul, the clan of the Shaulites.
These are the families of Simeon, and their number was 22,200.
The sons of Judah were Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. Er and Onan died in the land of Canaan.
And the descendants of Judah, according to their families, were: from Shelah, the clan of the Shelanites; from Perez, the clan of the Perezites; and from Zerah, the clan of the Zerahites.
And the descendants of Perez were: from Hezron, the clan of the Hezronites; and from Hamul, the clan of the Hamulites.
These are the families of Judah, and their number was 76,500.
And the descendants of Issachar, according to their families: from Tola, the clan of the Tolaites; and from Puah, the clan of the Puhites.
From Jashub, the clan of the Jashubites; and from Shimron, the clan of the Shimronites.
These are the families of Issachar, and their number was 74,400.
And the descendants of Zebulun, according to their families: from Sered, the clan of the Seredites; from Elon, the clan of the Elonites; and from Jahleel, the clan of the Jahleelites.
These are the families of Zebulun, and their number was 70,500.
And the descendants of Gad, according to their families: from Zephon, the clan of the Zephonites; from Haggi, the clan of the Haggites; and from Shuni, the clan of the Shunites.
From Azen came the Azenite clan, and from Sad came the Sadite clan.
From Arod, the clan of the Arodites; and from Areli, the clan of the Arelites.
These are the families of Gad, and their number was 44,500.
And the descendants of Asher, according to their families: from Jimnah, the clan of the Jimnites; from Ishvi, the clan of the Ishvites; and from Beriah, the clan of the Beriites.
From Heber, the clan of the Heberites; and from Malchiel, the clan of the Malchielites.
And the name of Asher’s daughter was Serah.
These are the families of Asher, and their number was 43,700.
And the descendants of Joseph, according to their families, were Manasseh and Ephraim.
And the descendants of Manasseh: from Machir, the clan of the Machirites. And Machir fathered Gilead.
From Gilead, the clan of the Gileadites.

These are the descendants of Gilead: from Ahiezer, the clan of the Ahiezerites; from Helek, the clan of the Helekites; from Asriel, the clan of the Asrielites; and from Shechem, the clan of the Shechemites.
From Shemida, the clan of the Shemidaites; and from Hepher, the clan of the Hepherites.
And Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, had no sons, only daughters. And these are their names: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
These were the people of Manasseh, and their number was 52,700.
And these are the descendants of Ephraim: from Shuthelah, the clan of the Shuthelahites; and from Tahan, the clan of the Tahanites.
These are the descendants of Shuthelah: from Eran, the clan of the Eranites.
These are the people of Ephraim, and their number was 32,500. These are the people descended from Joseph, according to their clans.
The descendants of Benjamin, according to their clans: from Bela, the clan of the Belaites; from Ashbel, the clan of the Ashbelites; and from Ahiram, the clan of the Ahiramites.
And from Shupham, the clan of the Shuphamites.
The sons of Bela were Ard and Naaman, the clan of the Naamites.
These are the descendants of Benjamin according to their clans, and their number was 45,700.
The sons of Dan, according to their clans: from Shuham came the Shuhamite clan. These were the people of Dan according to their clans.
The number of all the clan of Shuham was 74,700.
The descendants of Naphtali, according to their clans: from Jahzeel, the clan of the Jahzeelites; and from Guni, the clan of the Gunites.
And from Jezer, the clan of the Jezerites; and from Shillem, the clan of the Shillemites.
These are the people of Naphtali, and their number was 45,400.
This was the number of the Israelites: 601,730.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
These shall inherit that land according to their allotted portions and according to the number of their names.

For those who are more numerous, make their allotted share larger, and for those who are fewer, make their allotted share smaller. Give each of them their allotted share in proportion to their number.
Their allotted portions shall come to them by lot, to those named according to the clans of their fathers.
They shall inherit from their allotted portions, receiving their inheritance among the many and the few.
The descendants of Levi, according to their clans: from Gershon, the clan of the Gershonites; from Kohath, the clan of the Kohathites; and from Merari, the clan of the Merarites.
These are the people of the clans descended from Levi: the clan of the Libnites, the clan of the Hebronites, the clan of the Mushites, and the clan of the Korahites. Kohath fathered Amram.
The name of Amram’s wife was Jochebed, Levi’s daughter, whom [?] bore to Levi in the land of Egypt. She bore Aaron, Moses, and their sister Miriam to Amram.
Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar were born to Aaron.
Nadab and Abihu died when they brought unauthorized fire before the Lord in the wilderness of Sinai.
Their number was 23,000, every male one month old and older. They were not counted with the Israelites, because no allotted portion was given to them among the Israelites.
This was the census taken by Moses and Eleazar the priest, who counted the Israelites on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
Among these, not one man remained of those whom Moses and Aaron had counted when they counted the Israelites in the wilderness of Sinai.
For the Lord had told them that they would certainly die in the wilderness. Not one of them remained except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun.

The daughters of Zelophehad came forward. He was the son of Hepher, son of Gilead, son of Machir, from the tribe of Manasseh, among the descendants of Joseph. These were their names: Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.
They stood before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, before the leaders, and before the whole assembly at the entrance to the tent of testimony, and said:
Our father died in the wilderness. He was not among the assembly that rose up against the Lord in Korah’s assembly. Rather, he died for his own sin, and he had no sons.
Let our father’s name not be erased from among his clan because he had no son. Give us our allotted share among our father’s brothers.
Moses brought their words before the Lord.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
The daughters of Zelophehad have spoken rightly. Give them their allotted inheritance among their father’s brothers, and transfer their father’s allotted portion to them.
Tell the Israelites and say to them, “If a man dies and has no sons, you shall give his inheritance to his daughters.
If he has no daughter, give his inheritance to his brothers.
If he has no brothers, give his inheritance to his father’s brothers.”

If his father has no brothers, give his inheritance to his nearest relative’s household within his clan, and he shall inherit it. This shall be a statute of my judgment for the Israelites, as the Lord commanded Moses.
The Lord said to Moses, “Go up the mountain on the far side, namely Mount Nebo, and look at the land of Canaan, which I am giving the Israelites to possess.
See it, and then you too shall be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron was gathered on Mount Hor.

For you disobeyed my command in the wilderness of Zin when you quarreled with the assembly, and you did not acknowledge my holiness before them concerning the water. These are the waters of contention at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin.”
Moses said to the Lord:
Let the Lord, the God of every soul and all flesh, appoint a man for this assembly,
who will go out and come in before them, who will lead them out and bring them in, so that the Lord’s assembly will not be like sheep without a shepherd.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him, “Take Joshua son of Nun, a man upon whom the Holy Spirit rests, and lay your hand on him.
Have him stand before Eleazar the priest, and give him instructions before the whole assembly. Issue commands concerning him in their presence.
Confer your authority upon him so that the Israelites will obey him.

He shall stand before Eleazar the priest, and they shall ask him for the judgment pronounced before the Lord. At his command they shall go out, and at his command they shall come in—he and the Israelites together, and the whole assembly.”
Moses did as the Lord commanded him. He took Joshua and had him stand before Eleazar the priest and before the whole assembly.
He laid his hand on him and appointed him, as the Lord commanded.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
Command the Israelites and say to them: Take care to bring me my offering, my gift, and my sacrifices of a pleasing aroma at my appointed festivals.
“Say to them, ‘This is my offering, which you shall bring to the Lord: two year-old lambs without blemish each day as a regular offering.
You shall offer one lamb in the morning, and you shall offer one lamb toward evening.
You shall prepare a tenth of an ephah of fine flour for the regular offering, mixed with a quarter of a hin of oil,
as the regular offering that was made on Mount Sinai, for a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
Its drink offering shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb. Pour out the drink offering in the holy place to the Lord.
They shall offer the second lamb toward evening. You shall prepare it with its offering and its drink offering, for a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the Sabbath day you shall offer two year-old lambs without blemish, and two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, together with its drink offering.
This is the Sabbath offering for each Sabbath, in addition to the regular offering and its drink offering.
At the beginning of the month you shall bring an offering to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs.
For each bull, three-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil; and for the one ram, two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil;
and for each lamb, a tenth of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil—an offering for a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

Their drink offerings shall be half a hin for each bull, a third of a hin for the one ram, and a quarter of a hin of wine for each lamb. This is the offering for each month, month after month throughout the months of the year.’
And offer one male goat to the Lord as a sin offering, in addition to the regular offering and its drink offering.
In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month, is the Lord’s Passover.
On the fifteenth day of that month there shall be a festival; for seven days you shall eat unleavened bread.
The first day shall be called holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work.
You shall bring an offering to the Lord: two bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven lambs. They shall be one year old and without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil:
three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
You shall offer one tenth for each lamb, the same for all seven lambs.
And offer one male goat as a sin offering, through which atonement shall be made for you.
This is in addition to the offering made every morning as the regular offering.
You shall do this each day for seven days, a sacrificial offering of a pleasing aroma to the Lord, in addition to the regular sacrifice. You shall also make the drink offering.
The seventh day shall be holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work on it.
On the day of firstfruits, when you bring an offering of firstfruits to the Lord, you shall have a holy Sabbath. You shall do no ordinary work.
You shall bring an offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord: two young bulls from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull, two tenths for each ram, and one tenth for each lamb, the same for all seven lambs.
And offer one male goat as a sin offering, through which atonement shall be made for you.
You shall offer these to me in addition to the regular offering and their grain offerings. They shall be without blemish, and their drink offerings shall also be offered.
In the seventh month, at the beginning of the month, that day shall be called holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work on it, and it shall be a day of signaling for you.
You shall offer a sacrifice of a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull from the herd, one ram, and seven lambs, each one year old and without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
And one tenth for each lamb, the same for all seven lambs.
And offer one male goat as a sin offering, through which atonement shall be made for you.

This is in addition to the offering at the beginning of each month, with its grain offerings and drink offerings, and the regular offering, with its grain offerings and drink offerings, according to their prescribed rules, as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
On the tenth day of that month, the day shall be called holy for you. You shall afflict yourselves and do no ordinary work.
You shall bring an offering as a pleasing aroma: one young bull from the herd, one ram, and seven year-old lambs. They shall be without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be fine flour mixed with oil: three tenths for each bull and two tenths for each ram.
And one tenth for each lamb, the same for all seven lambs.

And offer one male goat as a sin offering, through which atonement shall be made for you, in addition to the sin offering of atonement and the regular offering, with their grain offerings and drink offerings, according to their prescribed rules, as a pleasing aroma.
On the fifteenth day of that seventh month, the day shall be called holy for you. You shall do no ordinary work, and you shall celebrate a festival to the Lord for seven days.
And bring a sacrificial offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord on the first day: three bulls from the cattle and ten cattle, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs. They must be without blemish.
Their grain offering shall be three tenths of fine flour mixed with oil for each bull, the same for all thirteen, and two tenths for each ram, the same for both rams.
One tenth for each lamb, the same for all fourteen lambs.
And one male goat from the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and its drink offerings and grain offerings.
On the second day: twelve bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, each one year old and without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
On the third day: eleven bulls, two rams, and fourteen lambs, each one year old and without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their respective numbers, as prescribed for them.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And on the fourth day: ten bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their respective numbers, as prescribed for them.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And on the fifth day: nine bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their number, as prescribed for them.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And on the sixth day: eight bulls, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their respective numbers and as prescribed for them.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And on the seventh day: seven cattle, two rams, and fourteen year-old lambs without blemish.
And also their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their respective numbers and as prescribed for them.
And one young goat from among the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and their sacrifices and drink offerings.
And the eighth day shall be a day of assembly for you. You shall do no laborious work on it.
And bring a sacrificial offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord: one bull and one ram for sacrifice, and seven year-old lambs without blemish.
And their grain offerings and drink offerings for the cattle, the rams, and the lambs shall be according to their respective numbers and as prescribed for them.
And one male goat from the goats as a sin offering, besides the regular sacrifice and its grain offerings and drink offerings.
And do this for the Lord at your festivals, along with your voluntary offerings, your offerings, your sacrifices, your drink offerings, and your peace offerings.
And Moses told the Israelites everything that the Lord had commanded Moses.
And Moses spoke to the leaders of the people of Israel and said to them, “This is the word that the Lord has commanded.”
If any man makes a vow to the Lord, swears an oath, or undertakes an obligation to abstain, he shall not break his word. He shall do everything that has come out of his mouth.
And if a woman makes a vow to the Lord or undertakes an obligation to abstain while she is young and in her father's house,

and her father hears her prayer and all the vows she has undertaken for herself, and her father remains silent, then all her prayer shall remain binding upon her, and all the vows she has undertaken for herself shall remain binding upon her.

But if her father [?] her and puts an end to it for her on the day he hears, none of her prayer or the vows she has undertaken for herself shall remain binding upon her. And the Lord shall absolve her on the day her father [?] her.
And if she marries a man while bound by a vow she has spoken with her lips, by anything she has pledged concerning herself,
and her husband hears of it and remains silent on the day he hears, all her vows shall remain binding on her, and the pledges she has made concerning herself shall remain binding on her.

But if her husband objects to her and revokes them on the day he hears, none of her vows or the pledges she has made concerning herself shall remain binding on her, because her husband has objected to her, and the Lord shall release her from guilt.
But the vow of a widow or of a woman whose husband has divorced her—everything she has pledged concerning herself—shall remain binding on her.
And if she makes a vow and a pledge concerning herself while living in her husband's house,
and her husband hears and remains silent, without objecting to her, all her vows shall remain binding on her, and all the pledges she has made concerning herself shall remain binding on her.

But if her husband objects to her and revokes them on the day he hears, nothing that has come from her lips, whether a vow or a pledge concerning herself, shall remain binding on her, because her husband has objected to her, and the Lord shall release her from guilt.
Every pledge and every binding oath that brings hardship upon her, her husband may confirm for her, or her husband may oppose.
But if he remains silent toward her from day to day, he confirms all her vows as binding on her, and he also confirms her pledges as binding on her, because he remained silent on the day he heard.
But if he does this to her after the day on which he heard it, he will bear the guilt.
These are all the regulations that the Lord commanded Moses concerning a man and his wife, and a father and his daughter while she is young and living in her father's house.
And the Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Take vengeance on the Midianites for the Israelites, and afterward you shall be gathered to your people.”
And Moses spoke to the people and said to them, “Equip men from among you, and fight before the Lord against Midian, so that they may bring the Lord's vengeance upon Midian.
Send a thousand from each tribe, a thousand from every tribe of Israel, to fight.”
And they counted out from the thousands of Israel a thousand from each tribe, making twelve thousand men equipped for battle.
And Moses sent them out, a thousand from each tribe, with their forces, and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron the priest, with the sacred vessels and the signaling trumpets accompanying them.
And they fought against Midian, as the Lord had commanded Moses, and killed all their males.
They also killed the kings of Midian along with the others they killed: Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba, the five kings of Midian. They also killed Balaam son of Beor with the sword in that slaughter.
And they took the women of Midian captive, and seized their possessions, their livestock, all their property, and their wealth.
And they burned with fire all the towns where they lived, and their settlements.
And they took all their captives and their plunder, both people and animals.
And they brought the captives, the plunder, and what they had looted to Moses, to Eleazar the priest, and to all the Israelites, at the camp on the plains of Moab beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
And Moses, Eleazar the priest, and all the leaders of the camp went out to meet them outside the camp.
And Moses became furious with the officers of the army, their commanders, and the officers who had returned from the fighting on the battlefield.
And Moses said to them, “Why have you kept all the women alive?”
For these are the women who, as Balaam directed, led the Israelites astray and made them abandon the word of the Lord in the affair of Peor, and the Lord's plague came upon the camp.
And now kill every male wherever they are, and kill every woman who has had sexual relations with a man.
But keep alive all the girls who have not had sexual relations with a man.
But you must camp outside the camp for seven days. Everyone who has killed someone or touched a dead body must purify himself on the third day and on the seventh day, both you and your captives.
Purify every garment, every leather article, every article made from goatskin, and every wooden object.
Eleazar said to the soldiers who had returned from the battle where they had been fighting, “This is the requirement of the law that the Lord commanded Moses:
Gold, silver, bronze, iron, lead, and tin—
Every utensil that is worked by fire and becomes clean must be purified with the water of purification, and everything that goes into fire must be immersed in water.
Wash your clothes on the seventh day, and you will be clean. After this you may enter the camp.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said:
“Take an inventory of the captives and the plunder, both people and animals—you, Eleazar, and the representatives of the ancestral families of the congregation.
Divide the plunder between the warriors who went out to fight and the whole congregation.
Set aside a tribute for the Lord from the warriors who went out to fight: one living being out of every five hundred, from the people, the animals, the cattle, the sheep, and the donkeys.
Take it from their half and give it to Eleazar the priest as the Lord’s firstfruits.

From the Israelites’ half, take one out of every fifty, from the people, the cattle, the sheep, the donkeys, and the animals. Give them to the Levites who carry out the duties of the Lord’s tabernacle.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The number of sheep captured by the men who fought was 675,000.
Their cattle numbered 72,000.
There were 71,000 donkeys.
And the human beings of the female sex who had not known a man numbered 32,000 persons in all.
The half-share belonging to those who went to war amounted to 337,500 sheep.
And the tribute for the Lord from the sheep was 775.
There were 36,000 cattle, and the tribute for the Lord was 72.
There were 30,500 donkeys, and the tribute for the Lord was 61.
There were 16,000 living people, and the tribute for the Lord was 32.
And Moses gave the tribute for the Lord, which they had set aside for the Lord, to Eleazar the priest, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
From the Israelites’ half, which Moses separated from the men who went to war:
The half belonging to the congregation amounted to 337,500 sheep.
There were 36,000 cattle.
There were 30,500 donkeys.
There were 16,000 living people.
Moses took one out of every fifty people and animals from the Israelites’ half and gave them to the Levites, who carried out the duties of the Lord’s tabernacle, as the Lord had commanded Moses.
And all those appointed over the army, the army commanders and officers, came to Moses.
They said to Moses, “Your men have taken the ornaments of the men who fought with us, and not one of them is missing from us.

Look, we have brought an offering to the Lord, each man bringing whatever gold ornament he found—an armlet, a bracelet, a ring, or a braided necklace—so that you may make atonement for us before the Lord.”
Moses and Eleazar the priest received the gold from them, all of it made into ornaments.
All the gold of the offering that they set apart for the Lord, from the army commanders and the officers, amounted to [?] shekels.
The men who had fought brought in the plunder they had taken, each for himself.
And Moses and Eleazar the priest took that gold from the army commanders and officers and brought it into the tent of testimony as a memorial for the Israelites.
The descendants of Reuben had many livestock, and the descendants of Gad had very many indeed. They saw that the lands of Jazer and Gilead were suitable for livestock.
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad came and spoke to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the leaders of the congregation, saying,
“Ataroth, Dibon, Jazer, Nimrah, Heshbon, Elealeh, Sibmah, Nebo, and Beon—
the land that the Lord has given before the Israelites is a land for grazing livestock, and we your servants have many livestock.”
They said to him, “If we have found favor with you, give this land to your servants as our allotted possession, and do not make us cross the Jordan.”
Moses said to the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad, “Are your brothers to go and fight while you stay here?
Why are you discouraging the Israelites from going into the land that the Lord is giving them?
Is this not what your fathers did when I sent them from Kadesh to inspect that land?
They went up to the Valley of Eshcol to inspect the land, and they turned the hearts of the Israelites away from entering the land that the Lord was giving them.
The Lord’s anger flared up that day, and he swore, saying,

“These men who came out of Egypt, those among them who were twenty years old and older and knew good and evil, shall not see the land that the Lord swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, because they did not follow me.”
“Except Caleb son of Jephunneh, who was set apart, and Joshua son of Nun, because they followed the Lord.
And the Lord’s anger burned against Israel, and he made them wander in the wilderness for forty years, until all that generation who did evil before the Lord had perished.
And now you have risen in your fathers’ place, a brood of sinful men, to add still more anger to the Lord’s anger against Israel.
For if you abandon him, you will cause him to abandon them in the wilderness again, and you will bring disaster on this whole congregation.”
They came near him and said, “Let us build sheepfolds here for our livestock and towns for our possessions.
“But we will go fully equipped with our weapons ahead of the Israelites until we bring them to their place. Our possessions will remain in fortified towns because of the inhabitants of the land.”
We will not return to our homes until the Israelites have received their inheritances, each his own.
We will not share an inheritance with them across the Jordan or beyond it, because we have received our share on the side of the Jordan toward the east.”
And Moses said to them, “If you do as you say and go with your weapons before the Lord into battle,
And all of you who carry your weapons of war must cross the Jordan before the Lord.
After this you may return, and you will be free of obligation before the Lord and toward Israel. This land will be your allotted possession before the Lord.
But if you do not do this, you will sin before the Lord, and when disaster overtakes you, you will recognize your sin.
Build cities for your dependents and enclosures for your livestock, and do what you have promised.
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad said to Moses, “We, your servants, will do as you have commanded us, my lord.”
“Our dependents and our wives will remain in the cities of Gilead, together with all our livestock.”
“But we will all go, equipped with our weapons, arrayed before the Lord for battle, as you say to us, my lord.”
And Moses appointed over them Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the ancestral families of the tribes of Israel.

Moses said to them, “If the descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad cross the Jordan with you, all equipped with their weapons for battle before the Lord, you will take this land that lies before you, and you shall give them Gilead as their allotted possession.”

“But if they do not cross over with you, equipped with their weapons, into battle before the Lord, bring their possessions, their wives, and their livestock across ahead of you into the land of Canaan.”
The descendants of Reuben and the descendants of Gad answered, “We will do everything our lord has told us.”
“We will cross over with our weapons before the Lord into the land of Canaan, and give us our allotted portion on the other side of the Jordan.”

Moses gave the descendants of Gad, the descendants of Reuben, and the half-tribe of Manasseh, the descendants of Joseph, the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites and the kingdom of Og king of Bashan—their land and their cities, together with their mountains and the cities in the surrounding land.
The descendants of Gad built Dibon, Ataroth, and Aroer;
and Shophan and Jazer;
and Nimrah and Beth-haran, fortified cities. They fortified them and built enclosures for sheep.
The descendants of Reuben built Heshbon, Elealeh, and Kiriathaim.
And Baal-meon and their fortifications and Sibmah; and they gave names to the towns they had built.
The son of Machir, son of Manasseh, went and captured Gilead and destroyed the Amorites who lived there.
Moses gave Gilead to Machir son of Manasseh, and he settled there.
Jair son of Manasseh went and captured their villages and named them the Villages of Jair.
And Nobah went and captured Kenath and its villages, and named them Nobah after himself.
These are the camps of the Israelites after they came out of Egypt with their forces under the leadership of Moses and Aaron.
Moses recorded their camps as they moved on, at the Lord’s command. These are the camps of their journey.
They set out from Rameses in the first month, on the fifteenth day of the first month. On the day after the Passover, the Israelites went out with uplifted hand in the sight of all Egypt.
And there were Egyptians burying their dead, all those whom the Lord had killed, every firstborn in the land of Egypt. The Lord also took vengeance on their gods.
The Israelites set out from Rameses and camped at Succoth.
They set out from Succoth and camped at Buthan, which is a part of the wilderness.
They set out from Buthan and camped at Pi-hahiroth, opposite Baal-zephon. They camped in front of Migdol.
They set out from before Hahiroth and crossed through the middle of the sea into the wilderness. They traveled for three days in the wilderness and camped at Marah.
They set out from Marah and arrived at Elim. At Elim there were twelve springs of water and seventy date palms, and they camped there beside the water.
They set out from Elim and camped beside the Red Sea.
They set out from the Red Sea and camped in the wilderness of Sin.
They set out from the wilderness of Sin and camped at Dophkah.
They set out from Dophkah and camped at Alush.
They set out from Alush and camped at Rephidim, where there was no water for the people to drink.
And they set out from Rephidim and camped in the wilderness of Sinai.
They set out from the wilderness of Sinai and camped at the Memorial of Craving.
They set out from the Memorial of Craving and camped at Hazeroth.
They set out from Hazeroth and camped at Rithmah.
They set out from Rithmah and camped at Rimmon-perez.
They set out from Rimmon-perez and camped at Libnah.
They set out from Libnah and camped at Rissah.
They set out from Rissah and camped at Kehelathah.
They set out from Kehelathah and camped at Mount Shepher.
They set out from Mount Shepher and camped at Haradah.
They set out from Haradah and camped at Makheloth.
They set out from Makheloth and camped at Tahath.
And they set out from Tahath and camped at Terah.
And they set out from Terah and camped at Mithkah.
They set out from Mithkah and camped at Hashmonah.
They set out from Hashmonah and camped at Moseroth.
They set out from Moseroth and camped at Bene-jaakan.
They set out from Bene-jaakan and camped at Mount Gidgad.
They set out from Mount Gidgad and camped at Jotbathah.
They set out from Jotbathah and camped at Abronah.
They set out from Abronah and camped at Ezion-geber.
They set out from Ezion-geber and camped in the wilderness of Zin. They set out from the wilderness of Zin and camped in the wilderness of Paran, which is Kadesh.
They set out from Kadesh and camped at Mount Hor, beside the land of Edom.
Aaron the priest went up at the LORD’s command and died there in the fortieth year after the Israelites came out of Egypt, on the first day of the fifth month.
Aaron was 123 years old when he died on Mount Hor.
The Canaanite king of Arad, who lived in the land of Canaan, heard that the Israelites were coming.
They set out from Mount Hor and camped at Zalmonah.
They set out from Zalmonah and camped at Punon.
They set out from Punon and camped at Oboth.
They set out from Oboth and camped at Gai, beyond the border of Moab.
They set out from Gai and camped at Dibon-gad.
They set out from Dibon-gad and camped at Almon-diblathaim.
And they set out from Almon-diblathaim and camped in the mountains of Abarim, opposite Nebo.
They set out from the mountains of Abarim and camped in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
They camped beside the Jordan, from Jeshimoth to Abel-shittim, in the plains of Moab.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan, opposite Jericho, and said to him:
“Speak to the Israelites and tell them: Look, you are crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
Destroy all the inhabitants of that land before you, demolish their works, destroy all their gods, and tear down all their images.
Wipe out those who live in that land and settle in it, for I have given you their land as your allotted possession.

You shall inherit that land and divide it among your tribes. Give a larger share to those who are more numerous and a smaller share to those who are fewer. Whatever falls to each one by name shall belong to him there. Divide it among your tribes and your ancestral households.

But if you do not destroy the inhabitants of that land before you, those whom you leave alive will become thorns in your eyes and prickles in your sides, and they will oppose you in the land where you live.
What I intended to do to them, I will do to you.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Command the Israelites and tell them: Look, you are entering the land of Canaan. It shall be your inheritance, within its borders.
Your southern side shall extend from the wilderness of Zin as far as the border of Edom. Your southern boundary shall begin at the eastern side of the Salt Sea.
Your southern boundary shall turn from the ascent of Akrabbim and reach as far as Senak. Its endpoint shall be south of Kadesh-barnea; it shall enter the towns of Arad and go out through Azmon.
The boundary shall turn from Azmon to the river of Egypt, and its endpoint shall be the sea.
For your western boundary, the Great Sea shall be your limit. This shall be your western boundary.
This shall be your northern boundary: from the Great Sea it shall be marked out for you toward the mountain.
From mountain to mountain, the boundary shall be marked out for you, reaching as far as Hamath, and its endpoint shall be the border of Zedad.
The boundary shall go out to Ziphron, and its endpoint shall be [?] Hazar-enan. This shall be your northern boundary.
Your eastern boundary shall be marked out for you from Hazar-enan [?] Shepham.
Your boundary shall descend from Shepham as far as Arbela and meet the eastern shore of the Sea of Chinnereth.”
The boundary shall descend to the Jordan, and its endpoint shall be the Salt Sea. This shall be your land, with its boundaries all around it.
Moses spoke to the Israelites and said to them, “This is your land, which you shall inherit and divide, as the Lord commanded that it be given to the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
For the tribe of the descendants of Reuben and the tribe of the descendants of Gad, according to their ancestral households, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have received their allotted possession.”
The two tribes and the half-tribe took possession of their allotment beyond the Jordan, opposite Jericho, on its eastern side.
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“These are the names of the men who will divide the land among you: Eleazar the priest and Joshua son of Nun.
Take one representative from each tribe to allot that land to you as your inheritance.
These are the names of those men: from the tribe of Judah, Caleb son of Jephunneh;
from the tribe of Simeon, Shelumiel son of Ammihud;
from the tribe of Benjamin, Eldad son of Chislon;
from the tribe of Dan, Bukki son of Jogli, a leader;
from the descendants of Joseph, from the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, Hanniel son of Suphid, a leader;
from the tribe of the descendants of Ephraim, Kemuel son of Shiphtan, a leader;
from the tribe of the descendants of Zebulun, Elizaphan son of Parnach, a leader;
from the tribe of the descendants of Issachar, Paltiel son of Azzan, a leader;
From the tribe of the descendants of Asher, the representative shall be Ahihud son of Shelomi.
from the tribe of the descendants of Naphtali, Pedahel son of Ammihud, a leader.”
These are the men whom the Lord commanded to measure out the land of Canaan for Israel.
The Lord spoke to Moses in the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho, and said to him:
“Command the Israelites to give the Levites towns to live in from the allotments they will inherit. They must also give the Levites the surrounding lands of those towns.
They will have the towns to live in, and their fields will be for their cattle and their other animals.
The boundaries of the towns you give the Levites are to be measured outward from the town, all around it:

two thousand cubits from the eastern edge of the town, two thousand cubits from its southern side, two thousand cubits from its western side, and two thousand cubits from its northern side. The town is to be in the middle of this area for you, and likewise their other towns.
You must give the Levites six cities of refuge, which you will set apart so that a person who has killed someone may find refuge there. Besides these, you must give them forty-two other towns.
All the towns you give the Levites will total forty-eight, and these towns are to come with their surrounding lands.

The towns you give from the Israelites’ allotments must be many from those who have much and few from those who have little. Each of them must give the Levites towns from the inheritance allotted to them.”
The Lord spoke to Moses and said to him:
“Tell the Israelites and say to them: ‘You are now crossing the Jordan into the land of Canaan.
Set apart cities of refuge for yourselves, so that anyone who has killed a person unintentionally may flee there.
Those cities shall be places of refuge for you from the avenger of blood, so that the killer does not die before standing before the assembly and being tried.
The cities you give are to be six cities of refuge for you.’
Set apart three cities beyond the Jordan, and set apart three cities in the land of Canaan.
They shall be a refuge for the Israelites, for the resident foreigner, and for the immigrant living among you.
These cities shall be a refuge for them, so that anyone who has killed a person unintentionally may flee there.
But if someone strikes another with an iron implement and that person dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
If he strikes someone with a stone or drops it on him from his hand, and that person dies, he is a murderer. The one who killed shall surely be put to death.
And if someone strikes another with a wooden implement and that person dies, or drops something from his hand onto him and he dies, he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death.
The avenger of blood himself shall kill him.
And if someone hates another and throws any object onto him while lying in wait for him, and he dies,
he is a murderer. They shall put the person who struck him to death, because he is a murderer. The murderer must be put to death, and the avenger of blood shall kill him wherever he finds him.
But if it happens suddenly, without hatred, and someone throws any object onto another without lying in wait for him,
Or if he kills someone unknowingly with any stone that causes his death, without being his enemy or intending to harm him;
The assembly shall judge between the killer and the avenger of blood according to this law.

the assembly shall rescue the killer from the avenger of blood. The assembly shall bring him to the city of refuge where he takes shelter, and he shall remain there until the death of the high priest who was anointed with holy oil.
But if the killer goes outside the boundaries of the city where he took refuge,
and the avenger of blood finds him outside the boundaries of his city of refuge and kills him, the avenger of blood incurs no guilt.

For he must remain in his city of refuge until the high priest dies. After the high priest dies, he may return to the land he owns. This shall be your rule for judgment throughout your generations, wherever you live.
Anyone who has killed a person and against whom there is testimony—you shall put that murderer to death. But one witness shall not be sufficient evidence to put a person to death.
Do not accept a ransom for the life of a murderer whose crime deserves death. He must be put to death.
And do not accept a ransom to send him fleeing to a city of refuge so that he may live in the land again until the high priest dies.
Do not make the land where you live guilty of murder, for it is blood that makes the land guilty of murder. The land will not forgive the person who shed blood upon it.
Do not defile the land where you live and where I dwell with you, for I am the Lord who dwells among the Israelites.

The leaders of the clan of the ancestral house of Gilead son of Machir, son of Manasseh, from the tribe of the descendants of Joseph, came and spoke before Moses, before Eleazar the priest, and before the leaders of the ancestral houses of the Israelites.

They said, “The Lord commanded our lord to give the Israelites the land of their inheritance according to their allotted portions. The Lord also commanded our lord to give the allotted portion of our brother Zelophehad to his daughters.

If they become the wives of men from one of the tribes of the Israelites, their allotted portion will be taken from the allotted portion of our ancestors and added to the allotted portion of another tribe into which they marry. It will be taken from our allotted inheritance.

If this happens, it will pass away from the Israelites, and their inheritance will become part of the inheritance of another tribe into which they marry. For then it will be taken from the inheritance and allotted portion of our ancestral tribe.”
Moses commanded the Israelites according to the Lord’s command and said to them, “For this is what the tribe of the descendants of Joseph has said.
This is what the Lord commanded the daughters of Zelophehad, saying: “Let them marry whoever pleases them, but let them marry within the tribe of their fathers.”
The inheritance of the Israelites shall not pass from tribe to tribe, for the Israelites shall each hold to the inheritance of their ancestors.
Every daughter among the Israelites who claims an inheritance shall marry someone from her own tribe, so that the Israelites may each claim the inheritance of their ancestors.
An inheritance shall not pass from one tribe to another. Instead, the Israelites shall each hold to their own allotted portion.”
The daughters of Zelophehad did as the Lord had commanded Moses.
The daughters of Zelophehad married sons of their relatives within the tribe of the descendants of Manasseh, the descendants of Joseph:
Mahlah, Tirzah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Noah. Their inheritance remained within the tribe of their ancestral clan.
These are the commandments, judgments, and laws that the Lord commanded through Moses on the plains of Moab, beside the Jordan opposite Jericho.
